source.text: Legends of Localization is an examination of the cultural influences and differences that affect Japanese and English games. This book is an educational, history-focused exploration of the Undertale video game, but this book is not official Undertale merchandise in any form.

translation.text: Legends of Localization 探讨影响日语与英语游戏的文化因素及差异。本书以教育和历史为出发点，研究电子游戏 Undertale，但并非任何形式的 Undertale 官方商品。

source.text: Certain portions of this book’s content (and the localization information on many other games) is freely available online at: http://LegendsOfLocalization.com

translation.text:
本书部分内容，以及许多其他游戏的本地化资料，可在以下网站免费阅读：

source.text: Introduction
source.raw: Introduction

translation.text: 引言

source.text: Have you ever played a video game, watched a movie, or read a book and wondered what it was like in its original language? Or have you ever wondered how your favorite game, movie, or book sounds in a different language? Welcome to the world of Legends of Localization!
source.raw:
Have you ever played a video game, watched a movie, or read a book and
wondered what it was like in its original language? Or have you ever wondered
how your favorite game, movie, or book sounds in a different language?
Welcome to the world of Legends ofLocalization!

translation.text: 你有没有在玩游戏、看电影或读书时，好奇过作品在原文里是什么样的？有没有想过，自己喜欢的游戏、电影或书换一种语言，会是什么感觉？欢迎来到《Legends of Localization》的世界！

source.text: In this book, we'll take a detailed look at the popular American video game known as Undertale. We'll compare the original English version of the game with its official Japanese release. We'll also look at some of the translation challenges involved, and the solutions that were used to overcome them.
source.raw:
In this book, we'll take a detailed look at the popular American video game
nown as Undertale. We'll compare the original English version of the game
ith its official Japanese release. We'll also look at some of the translation
hallenges involved, and the solutions that were used to overcome them.

translation.text: 本书将详细介绍广受欢迎的美国游戏 Undertale，比较它的英语原版与官方日语版，看看翻译中遇到了哪些难题，又是怎样解决的。

source.text: Along the way, we'll examine other related topics, such as:
source.raw: long the way, we'll examine other related topics, such as:

translation.text: 我们还会讨论一些相关话题，例如：

source.text: What "localization" is and how it differs from translation Undertale's history and the inspirations behind the game Undertale's localization process as seen from the inside Common problems and mistakes in entertainment localization How culture and language shape a game's localization and vice-versa How unofficial, volunteer-made localizations and official localizations interact, how they differ, and what they mean to fans
source.raw:
What "localization" is and how it differs from translation
Underta/e's history and the inspirations behind the game
Underta/e's localization process as seen from the inside
Common problems and mistakes in entertainment localization
How culture and language shape a game's localization and vice-versa
How unofficial, volunteer-made localizations and official localizations
interact, how they differ, and what they mean to fans

translation.text:
• 什么是“本地化”，它与翻译有什么不同
• Undertale 的历史与创作灵感
• Undertale 本地化的幕后过程
• 娱乐作品本地化中常见的问题与错误
• 文化、语言与游戏本地化之间的相互影响
• 志愿者制作的非官方译版与官方译版如何互动、有何不同，又对爱好者意味着什么

source.text: Some of this might sound like dry, boring academic material, but don't worry - it'll be a genuinely fun and enlightening journey. After all, how do bad knock knock jokes and skeleton puns even work in Japanese? Do they just get lost in translation? Let's find out!
source.raw:
Some of this might sound like dry, boring academic material, but don't worry -
it'll be a genuinely fun and enlightening journey. After all, how do bad knock
knock jokes and skeleton puns even work in Japanese? Do they just get lost in
translation? Let's find out!

translation.text: 有些话题听起来或许像枯燥的学术材料，不过别担心，读起来其实既有趣，又能让人长见识。那些蹩脚的敲门笑话和骷髅双关，到了日语里还能成立吗？还是会在翻译中丢失笑点？一起看看吧！

source.text: Newcomers Welcome
source.raw: Newcomers Welcome

translation.text: 欢迎新读者

source.text: Although this book analyzes the English and Japanese versions of Undertale and touches on topics that will surely delight Undertale fans, it's also been designed with general audiences in mind. Everything in this book is explained in clear, simple English for readers who know nothing about Undertale, video games, the Japanese language, or translation.
source.raw:
Although this book analyzes the English and Japanese versions of Undertale
and touches on topics that will surely delight Undertale fans, it's also been
designed with general audiences in mind. Everything in this book is explained
in clear, simple English for readers who know nothing about Undertale, video
games, the Japanese language, or translation.

translation.text: 本书分析 Undertale 的英日版本，也会谈到爱好者感兴趣的话题，但写作时同样考虑了普通读者。书中所有内容都用清楚易懂的英语讲解，即使不了解 Undertale、电子游戏、日语或翻译，也能读懂。

source.text: Basically, whatever your background is, you'll come away from this book with a deeper understanding of language, culture, and translation.
source.raw:
Basically, whatever your background is, you'll come away from this book with a
deeper understanding of language, culture, and translation.

translation.text: 无论你有怎样的背景，读完后都能对语言、文化和翻译有更深的了解。

source.text: If you don't know the first thing about games, translation, Japanese, or Undertale, no worries!

translation.text: 就算你对游戏、翻译、日语或 Undertale 一窍不通，也不用担心！

source.text: Concerning Spoilers
source.raw: Concerning Spoilers

translation.text: 关于剧透

source.text: Undertale is full of surprises, branching story routes, and endings. Every playthrough feels unique and memorable - especially your first one. For this reason, spoilers can greatly affect the gameplay experience.
source.raw:
Undertale is full of surprises, branching story routes, and endings. Every
playthrough feels unique and memorable - especially your first one. For this
reason, spoilers can greatly affect the gameplay experience.

translation.text: Undertale 充满惊喜、故事分支和不同结局。每次游玩都有独特而难忘的体验，第一次尤其如此。因此，剧透会大大影响游玩体验。

source.text: If you're already an Undertale fan, then you're probably familiar with the story's many twists. But if you've never played it before and plan to someday, keep in mind that portions of this book will naturally contain spoilers.
source.raw:
If you're already an Under tale fan, then you're probably familiar with the
story's many twists. But if you've never played it before and plan to someday,
keep in mind that portions of this book will naturally contain spoilers.

translation.text: 如果你已经是 Undertale 的爱好者，想必熟悉故事的种种转折。但如果你还没玩过，打算今后体验，就要注意：本书有些内容难免涉及剧透。

source.text: Although this book wasn't designed as a gameplay supplement, you probably could read through it as you play the game. Who knows, it could even add a new perspective to the gameplay experience!
source.raw:
Although this book wasn't designed as a gameplay supplement, you probably
could read through it as you play the game. Who knows, it could even add a
new perspective to the gameplay experience!

translation.text: 本书原本并不是供游玩时配合阅读的，不过你也可以试着边玩边读。说不定，还会让你从新的角度体验游戏！

source.text: About Me
source.raw: About Me

translation.text: 关于我

source.text: My name is Clyde Mandelin, but I'm more commonly known on line as "Tomato" or just "Mato". I'm a professional Japanese-to-English translator and have been in the industry for about twenty years. I specialize in translating Japanese movies, anime, games, and other entertainment into English.
source.raw:
My name is Clyde Mandelin, but I'm more commonly known on line as
"Tomato" or just "Mato". I'm a professional Japanese-to-English translator and
have been in the industry for about twenty years. I specialize in translating
Japanese movies, anime, games, and other entertainment into English.

translation.text: 我叫 Clyde Mandelin，不过大家在网上更熟悉的名字是“Tomato”，或简称“Mato”。我是一名职业日译英译者，从业约二十年，主要将日本电影、动画、游戏及其他娱乐作品译成英语。

source.text: During my journey to become a professional translator, I studied Japanese-to English translation in university, in Japan, and on my own as a hobby. As part of my hobby study, I translated old Japanese games that had never been released in English. In short, translation has been a major part of my personal life and professional life for decades.
source.raw:
During my journey to become a professional translator, I studied Japanese-to
English translation in university, in Japan, and on my own as a hobby. As part of
my hobby study, I translated old Japanese games that had never been released
in English. In short, translation has been a major part of my personal life and
professional life for decades.

translation.text: 在成为职业译者的过程中，我在大学、在日本，以及作为业余爱好自学过日译英。业余学习的一部分，是翻译从未推出英语版的日本老游戏。可以说，几十年来，翻译一直是我生活和工作的主要部分。

source.text: Several years ago, I started Legends of Localization, a website and a book series dedicated to explaining how popular games and movies change during the jump between languages. I've also written books about the history of bad video game translation and what happens when you try to let a computer translate an entire video game on its own.
source.raw:
Several years ago, I started Legends of Localization, a website and a book series
dedicated to explaining how popular games and movies change during the
jump between languages. I've also written books about the history of bad video
game translation and what happens when you try to let a computer translate an
entire video game on its own.

translation.text: 几年前，我创办了 Legends of Localization 网站和同名书系，介绍热门游戏、电影跨越语言时会发生什么变化。我还写过关于糟糕游戏翻译的历史，以及把整款游戏交给电脑自行翻译会发生什么的书。

source.text: Basically, I just really like translation and showing how the translation process works. Naturally, this detailed look at Undertale's Japanese translation is another passion project for me.
source.raw:
Basically, I just really like translation and showing how the translation process
works. Naturally, this detailed look at Underta/e's Japanese translation is
another passion project for me.

translation.text: 我就是很喜欢翻译，也很喜欢向大家展示翻译的过程。如此细看 Undertale 的日语翻译，自然又是一个出于热爱的项目。

source.text: From time to time, I'll share my thoughts and insights about Undertale, localization, business experiences, personal experiences, and so on. So keep your eyes out for the little tomato! Well, not literally "out". That would be weird.
source.raw:
From time to time, I'll share my thoughts and insights about Undertale,
localization, business experiences, personal experiences, and so on. So keep your
eyes out for the little tomato! Well, not literally "out". That would be weird.

translation.text: 我会不时分享自己对 Undertale、本地化的想法，以及工作和生活中的经历。所以，请留意那颗小番茄！英语里叫 keep your eyes out，可别真把眼睛“拿出来”，那也太奇怪了。

page.subtitle: 引言 · 私人学习译稿

source.text: A Rare Opportunity
source.raw: A Rare Opportunity

translation.text: 难得的机会

source.text: Because I specialize in Japanese-to-English translation, I usually write about how games are translated from Japanese into English. But Undertale gives us a chance to look at the opposite side of things: how English games are translated into Japanese.
source.raw:
Because I specialize in Japanese-to-English translation, I usually write about
how games are translated from Japanese into English. But Undertale gives us a
chance to look at the opposite side of things: how English games are translated
into Japanese.

translation.text: 我专做日译英，平时写的大多是日本游戏如何译成英语。不过，Undertale 让我们有机会从另一面看看：英语游戏如何译成日语。

source.text: In Legends of Localization Book 1, we looked at how the original Legend of Zelda was translated into English. There was one key issue, though - the game is so old that nobody remembers who the actual translator was or how the game's translation process worked. As a result, we could see how things changed in translation, but there was no way to ask why.

translation.text: 在《Legends of Localization》第1卷，我们研究了初代《The Legend of Zelda》如何译成英语。不过有个关键问题：游戏太老，已经没人记得究竟是谁翻译的，也没人记得翻译是怎么进行的。因此，我们看得见翻译改了什么，却无从追问为什么。

source.text: In Legends of Localization Book 2, we looked at how the classic game EarthBound was translated into English. Luckily, through personal connections and friendships, I was able to ask the game's creator and the game's head localizer a handful of questions. Given that EarthBound was twenty years old by then, I was thankful to receive any kind of inside information at all.

source.text: Before we dive into Undertale's English-to-Japanese localization, there's one big question that needs answering: what exactly is localization, anyway?

Before we dive into Underta/e's English-to-Japanese localization, there's one

source.text: The word "localization" is actually relatively new in the translation world, so different people use it to mean different things. Here's how I would define it in simple terms, though:
source.raw:
The word "localization" is actually relatively new in the translation world, so
different people use it to mean different things. Here's how I would define it in
simple terms, though:

translation.text: “本地化”在翻译界其实还是个相对年轻的词，不同的人用它表达不同的意思。简单来说，我会这样定义：

source.text: Basically, localization is translation. Localization just changes things a bit when a literal translation doesn't quite work.
source.raw:
Basically, localization is translation. Localization just changes things a bit
when a literal translation doesn't quite work.

translation.text: 本地化说到底就是翻译，只是在直译行不通的时候，稍微改动一下。

source.text: If you're unfamiliar with translation, this idea probably sounds odd at first. Why should anything be changed at all? Shouldn't a literal translation work all the time? Let's find out.
source.raw:
If you're unfamiliar with translation, this idea probably sounds odd at first.
Why should anything be changed at all? Shouldn't a literal translation work all
the time? Let's find out.

translation.text: 如果你不熟悉翻译，乍听之下可能觉得奇怪。为什么要改？难道不是任何时候都能直译吗？我们来看看。

source.text: Getting Literal
source.raw: Getting Literal

translation.text: 只按字面理解

source.text: Imagine you're talking to a grumpy genie who takes everything literally. You want to be rich, so you immediately wish to be "made of money". Unfortunately, instead of becoming rich, you transform into a pile of coins. Oops, that's not what you meant at all!
source.raw:

translation.text: 设想你遇到一个暴躁、凡事照字面理解的精灵。你想发财，立刻许愿让自己 made of money（富得流油，字面为“由钱构成”）。结果却变成了一堆硬币。哎呀，这可不是你想要的！

source.text: "Ugh, whatever! I just wish I had lots of dough!" you somehow say. You expect to become rich for sure this time, but instead, you suddenly find yourself covered in bread dough. Oops again!
source.raw:
"Ugh, whatever! I just wish I had lots of dough!" you somehow say. You expect
to become rich for sure this time, but instead, you suddenly find yourself
covered in bread dough. Oops again!

translation.text: “唉，随便吧！我只想要一大堆 dough！”不知怎么，你又开口了。dough 可以指“钱”，也可以指“面团”。你以为这次总该发财了，结果浑身糊满了面团。又糟了！

source.text: These examples, as ridiculous as they are, show how a literal interpretation can completely miss the point of what's being said.
source.raw:
These examples, as ridiculous as they are, show how a literal interpretation can
completely miss the point of what's being said.

translation.text: 这些例子虽然荒唐，却说明了按字面理解可以完全错过说话人的意思。

source.text: When we communicate, words are our tools. They're like paintbrushes that we use to paint pictures for others to see. The problem is that if you focus too hard on someone's tools, you risk missing the full picture of what they're actually saying.

page.subtitle: 什么是本地化？ · 私人学习译稿

source.text: The Need for Localization
source.raw: The Need for Localization

translation.text: 为什么需要本地化

source.text: Every language has its own unique rules and quirks. Every culture has its own unique values and expectations. Because of this, not every word has a perfect, 1-to-l equivalent in other languages. So when a straightforward, literal translation isn't possible, one alternative is to use completely different words to say the same thing. And that's precisely what localization is: preserving the creator's intended meaning but with completely different words. As the acclaimed translator John Ciardi once put it:
source.raw:
Every language has its own unique rules and quirks. Every culture has its
own unique values and expectations. Because of this, not every word has a
perfect, 1-to-l equivalent in other languages. So when a straightforward, literal
translation isn't possible, one alternative is to use completely different words
to say the same thing. And that's precisely what localization is: preserving the
creator's intended meaning but with completely different words. As the
acclaimed translator John Ciardi once put it:

translation.text: 每种语言都有自己的规则和特点，每种文化也有自己的价值观和预期。因此，并不是每个词都能在另一种语言中找到一一对应的词。无法直接照字面翻译时，一种办法就是换一套完全不同的说法，表达同样的意思。这正是本地化：用完全不同的词，保留创作者想表达的意思。正如著名译者 John Ciardi 所说：

source.text: '' When the violin repeats what the piano has just played, it cannot make the same sounds and it can only approximate the same chords. It can, however, make recognizably the same "music," the same air. But it can do so only when it is as faithful to the self logic of the violin as it is to the self logic of the piano.
source.raw:
'' When the violin repeats what the piano has just played, it cannot make the
same sounds and it can only approximate the same chords. It can, however~
mal<e recognizably the same "music," the same air. But it can do so only
when it is as faithfizl to the self logic of the violin as it is to the self logic of
the piano.

translation.text: 小提琴重复钢琴刚弹过的旋律时，发不出同样的声音，和弦也只能近似。不过，它仍能奏出听得出是同一段的“音乐”、同一支曲调。但要做到这一点，它既要忠实于钢琴自身的逻辑，也要同样忠实于小提琴自身的逻辑。

source.text: In short, languages are weird, messy, and complicated. It's easy for people to misunderstand each other in one language, so translating between two can sometimes be impossible. In this chapter, we'll examine a few situations in which straightforward, literal translations don't quite work.
source.raw:
In short, languages are weird, messy, and complicated. It's easy for people to
misunderstand each other in one language, so translating between two can
sometimes be impossible. In this chapter, we'll examine a few situations in
which straightforward, literal translations don't quite work.

translation.text: 总之，语言古怪、杂乱而复杂。用同一种语言，人们都容易误解彼此；在两种语言之间翻译，有时甚至是不可能的任务。本章将介绍一些直接照字面翻译不太行得通的情形。

source.text: Humor
source.raw: Humor

translation.text: 幽默

source.text: There's a famous joke in English that goes:
source.raw: There's a famous joke in English that goes:

translation.text: 英语里有个著名的笑话：

source.text: Why was 6 afraid of 7? Because 7 8 9!
source.raw: Why was 6 afraid of7 ? Because 7 8 9!

translation.text:
Why was 6 afraid of 7? Because 7 8 9!
6为什么怕7？因为7把9吃了！

source.text: Of course, this joke only works because the number "8" and the word "ate" share the same pronunciation in English. This isn't necessarily true in other languages, so a literal translation of the joke might sound like this:
source.raw:
Of course, this joke only works because the number "8" and the word "ate"
share the same pronunciation in English. This isn't necessarily true in other
languages, so a literal translation of the joke might sound like this:

translation.text: 这个笑话能成立，是因为英语里的数字“8”（eight）与“吃了”（ate）同音。其他语言未必如此，所以直译出来可能变成：

source.text: Why was the sixth digit afraid of the seventh digit? Because seventh digit eighth digit ninth digit!
source.raw:
Why was the sixth digit afraid oft he seventh digit? Because seventh digit
eighth digit ninth digit!

translation.text: 第六个数字为什么怕第七个数字？因为第七个数字、第八个数字、第九个数字！

source.text: As we can see, the result is meaningless nonsense that loses the original intention entirely. The joke is lost in translation.
source.raw:
As we can see, the result is meaningless nonsense that loses the original
intention entirely. The joke is lost in translation.

translation.text: 结果成了毫无意义的胡话，原本的用意完全丢失了。笑话就这样消失在翻译中。

source.text: Similarly, consider this Japanese joke:
source.raw: Similarly, consider this Japanese joke:

translation.text: 再看一个日语笑话：

source.text: ashi nihon aru kara nihonjin da
source.raw: ashi nihon aru kara nihonjin da

translation.text:
ashi nihon aru kara nihonjin da
我有两条腿，所以我是日本人。

source.text: This joke, translated literally, means "I have two legs, so I'm Japanese". Even though it's an incredibly simple, straightforward joke in Japanese, we can see how it makes zero sense when translated into English.
source.raw:
This joke, translated literally, means "I have two legs, so I'm Japanese". Even
though it's an incredibly simple, straightforward joke in Japanese, we can see
how it makes zero sense when translated into English.

translation.text: 直译就是“我有两条腿，所以我是日本人”（“两条”和“日本”都读 nihon）。它在日语里是很简单直接的笑话，译成英语却完全莫名其妙。

source.text: In short, humor rarely translates easily between languages.
source.raw: In short, humor rarely translates easily between languages.

translation.text: 总之，幽默很少能轻易跨越语言。

source.text: So, as a translator, what do you do when you run into an untranslatable joke? The most common solution is to take out the original joke and replace it with a similar joke that works in the target language. And that's precisely what localization is all about: retaining the original intent even if it means changing the original words.
source.raw:
So, as a translator, what do you do when you run into an untranslatable joke?
The most common solution is to take out the original joke and replace it with
a similar joke that works in the target language. And that's precisely what
localization is all about: retaining the original intent even if it means changing
the original words.

translation.text: 那么，译者遇到译不过去的笑话该怎么办？最常见的做法，是撤下原来的笑话，换上目标语言里能讲通的类似笑话。这正是本地化的要点：即使得改换原词，也要保留原本的用意。

source.text: Cultural Knowledge and Expectations
source.raw: Cultural Knowledge and Expectations

translation.text: 文化知识与预期

source.text: Have you ever heard someone tell an inside joke that you weren't in on? Even though you understood the literal words that were being said, the intended meaning was lost on you. This same thing happens in translation.
source.raw:
Have you ever heard someone tell an inside joke that you weren't in on? Even
though you understood the literal words that were being said, the intended
meaning was lost on you. This same thing happens in translation.

translation.text: 你有没有听过自己不懂的圈内笑话？每个字都听懂了，却不明白想表达什么。翻译也会遇到同样的情形。

source.text: Cultures are basically their own giant in-groups: they have their own histories, customs, rituals, traditions, folk stories, foods, and more. A reference to any of these might sound meaningless to an outsider when translated literally. In this situation, understanding the literal words isn't enough - the actual "inside joke" needs to be explained too. It basically needs to be translated twice instead of only once.
source.raw:
Cultures are basically their own giant in-groups: they have their own histories,

these might sound meaningless to an outsider when translated literally. In this

needs to be explained too. It basically needs to be translated twice instead of
only once.

translation.text: 每种文化都像一个巨大的圈子，有自己的历史、习俗、仪式、传统、民间故事、食物等。提及其中任何一项，直译给圈外人听都可能毫无意义。这时，理解字面还不够，也得解释那个“圈内笑话”。相当于要翻译两遍，而不是一遍。

source.text: There are several ways of handling cultural matters in translation. In academia, it's standard practice to translate everything literally and include lots of explanatory footnotes. In entertainment, it's more common to localize foreign cultural references by replacing them with something similar, but more familiar to the target audience

page.title: 说话方式
page.subtitle: 什么是本地化？ · 私人学习译稿

source.text: Speech Patterns
source.raw: Speech Patterns

translation.text: 说话方式

source.text: Naturally, a translator should strive to preserve what's being said. But it's often just as important to preserve how it's being said. Otherwise the resulting translation might become "flattened". A flattened translation lacks the original text's unique traits, can lead to confusion, and can cause key information to be lost.
source.raw:
Naturally, a translator should strive to preserve what's being said. But it's
often just as important to preserve how it's being said. Otherwise the resulting
translation might become "flattened". A flattened translation lacks the original
text's unique traits, can lead to confusion, and can cause key information to be
lost.

translation.text: 译者自然应尽力保留“说了什么”，但保留“怎么说”往往同样重要。否则，译文就可能被“磨平”：失去原文的独特之处，造成混淆，乃至丢掉关键信息。

source.text: Language-specific speech patterns are particularly tricky - and sometimes impossible - to preserve when jumping between languages. Here are a few speech patterns that can easily be lost in a literal translation.
source.raw:
Language-specific speech patterns are particularly tricky - and sometimes
impossible - to preserve when jumping between languages. Here are a few
speech patterns that can easily be lost in a literal translation.

translation.text: 某种语言独有的说话方式尤其难以跨越语言，有时根本无法保留。下面几种就很容易在直译中消失。

source.text: Accents and Dialects
source.raw: Accents and Dialects

translation.text: 口音与方言

source.text: Some speech patterns have their own histories, backgrounds, and deep ties to specific regions of specific countries. These speech patterns convey extra information that give off a specific vibe not found anywhere else.
source.raw:
Some speech patterns have their own histories, backgrounds, and deep ties
to specific regions of specific countries. These speech patterns convey extra
information that give off a specific vibe not found anywhere else.

translation.text: 有些说话方式有自己的历史、背景，并与特定国家的特定地区紧密相连。它们能传达额外信息，带出其他地方没有的独特感觉。

source.text: For example, there is no "Boston accent" in Japanese. There's no cowboy dialect, nor is there a "Southern belle" speech pattern. Similarly, there's no "Heian era" speech pattern or "Kyoto accent" in English. These speech patterns simply become flattened in a literal translation.
source.raw:
For example, there is no "Boston accent" in Japanese. There's no cowboy
dialect, nor is there a "Southern belle" speech pattern. Similarly, there's no
"Heian era" speech pattern or "Kyoto accent" in English. These speech patterns
simply become flattened in a literal translation.

translation.text: 例如，日语里没有“波士顿口音”，没有牛仔腔，也没有“美国南方淑女”的说话方式。同样，英语里没有“平安时代”的说话方式或“京都口音”。直译只会把这些特点磨平。

source.text: Pronouns
source.raw: Pronouns

translation.text: 代词

source.text: Different languages use pronouns in different ways. For example, in English we only have "I/me" when referring to ourselves, but there are dozens of ways to say "I" in Japanese, each with a different connotation.
source.raw:
Different languages use pronouns in different ways. For example, in English we
only have "I/me" when referring to ourselves, but there are dozens of ways to
say "I" in Japanese, each with a different connotation.

translation.text: 不同语言使用代词的方式不同。例如英语用来指自己的只有 I/me，而日语说“我”的方式有几十种，各有不同意味。

source.text: Similarly, there are dozens of Japanese pronouns that mean "you" in the singular, but it's just as common to restate the listener's name every time instead of using a pronoun. In fact, it's perfectly normal to drop pronouns entirely in Japanese if it's clear who's being referred to. The Japanese phrase for "I love you'', ai shiteiru, literally contains no pronouns, for instance.
source.raw:
Similarly, there are dozens of Japanese pronouns that mean "you" in the
singular, but it's just as common to restate the listener's name every time
instead of using a pronoun. In fact, it's perfectly normal to drop pronouns
entirely in Japanese if it's clear who's being referred to. The Japanese phrase
for "I love you'', ai shiteiru, literally contains no pronouns, for instance.

translation.text: 日语同样有几十个单数“你”的说法，但每次直接叫对方的名字、不用代词，也很常见。只要指的是谁足够明确，日语完全省略代词也很正常。例如 ai shiteiru（我爱你），字面上就没有任何代词。

source.text: Because every language uses pronouns in such different ways, dialogue and conversations risk being flattened when translated literally.
source.raw:
Because every language uses pronouns in such different ways, dialogue and
conversations risk being flattened when translated literally.

translation.text: 由于各语言使用代词的方式差异很大，直译对白和对话就可能磨平它们的特点。

source.text: Grammar
source.raw: Grammar

translation.text: 语法

source.text: The same sentence can flow very differently in different languages. For example, English sentences generally go subject-verb-object, as in "Bob ate a monkey". But in Japanese, sentences tend to go subject-object-verb, as in "Bob a monkey ate". This difference can make a literal translation fall apart when a sentence is incomplete - which is extremely common in Japanese - or when timing is important.
source.raw:
The same sentence can flow very differently in different languages. For
example, English sentences generally go subject-verb-object, as in "Bob ate a
monkey". But in Japanese, sentences tend to go subject-object-verb, as in "Bob
a monkey ate". This difference can make a literal translation fall apart when a
sentence is incomplete - which is extremely common in Japanese - or when
timing is important.

translation.text: 同一句话在不同语言里的行进顺序可能大不相同。例如英语通常是主语—动词—宾语，像 Bob ate a monkey（Bob 吃了一只猴子）；日语则通常是主语—宾语—动词，相当于“Bob 一只猴子吃了”。遇到不完整的句子——日语里极为常见——或讲究时机的台词，这种差异就可能让直译失效。

source.text: Other aspects of grnmmar, such as gendered speech and politeness levels, also get flattened in a literal translation. Basically, grammar is a language's rulebook, but not every language plays by the same rules.
source.raw:
Other aspects of grnmmar, such as gendered speech and politeness levels, also
get flattened in a literal translation. Basically, grammar is a language's rulebook,
but not every language plays by the same rules.

translation.text: 带有性别色彩的说话方式、礼貌程度等其他语法特点，也可能在直译中被磨平。语法就像一种语言的规则手册，但不是所有语言都按同一套规则行事。

page.title: 语言的独特之处
page.subtitle: 什么是本地化？ · 私人学习译稿

source.text: Language Peculiarities
source.raw: Language Peculiarities

translation.text: 语言的独特之处

source.text: Despite their differences, DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS tapes can all hold the same movie. These formats aren't compatible with each other, though - you can't just stick a VHS tape into a DVD player. Languages are very similar - they can say roughly the same things, but you can't just shove text from one language into another and hope it'll work right.
source.raw:
Despite their differences, DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS tapes can all hold the same
movie. These formats aren't compatible with each other, though - you can't
just stick a VHS tape into a DVD player. Languages are very similar - they can
say roughly the same things, but you can't just shove text from one language
into another and hope it'll work right.

translation.text: DVD、蓝光和 VHS 录像带虽各不相同，却都能装下同一部电影。不过，它们彼此并不兼容：你不能把 VHS 录像带塞进 DVD 播放器。语言也很相似，能表达大致相同的内容，却不能把一种语言的文字硬塞进另一种，就指望一切正常。

source.text: Here are some examples of how a language's uniqueness can cause literal translations to miss the mark.
source.raw:
Here are some examples of how a language's uniqueness can cause literal
translations to miss the mark.

translation.text: 下面几个例子说明，语言的独特之处如何让直译偏离原意。

source.text: Sound Effects
source.raw: Sound Effects

translation.text: 拟声词

source.text: Some sound-effect words, such as animal sounds, are generally easy to convert between languages. But some languages use sound-effect words more than others, and some languages have sound-effect words that don't even exist in other languages. For example, the Japanese language has a sound for staring. It even has a sound effect for silence. When it comes to sound effects, sometimes a literal translation isn't even possible.
source.raw:
Some sound-effect words, such as animal sounds, are generally easy to convert
between languages. But some languages use sound-effect words more than
others, and some languages have sound-effect words that don't even exist in
other languages. For example, the Japanese language has a sound for staring. It
even has a sound effect for silence. When it comes to sound effects, sometimes
a literal translation isn't even possible.

translation.text: 动物叫声之类的拟声词，通常很容易在语言之间转换。但有的语言比别的语言更常用这类词，有的语言还有别的语言根本没有的拟声、拟态词。例如日语有表示盯着看的“声音”，甚至连寂静也有“声音”。碰到这类词，有时连直译都不可能。

source.text: Punctuation
source.raw: Punctuation

translation.text: 标点

source.text: Not every language uses punctuation the same way. Some languages have similar-looking punctuation marks that serve different purposes. And some languages have punctuation marks that don't exist in other languages. Because of this, a literal translation with all of the original punctuation intact can have unintended effects.
source.raw:
Not every language uses punctuation the same way. Some languages have
similar-looking punctuation marks that serve different purposes. And some
languages have punctuation marks that don't exist in other languages. Because
of this, a literal translation with all of the original punctuation intact can have
unintended effects.

translation.text: 不是所有语言都以同样方式使用标点。有些标点看起来相似，用途却不同；有些标点在其他语言里根本不存在。因此，直译时照搬原来的全部标点，可能产生意料之外的效果。

source.text: Writing Systems
source.raw: Writing Systems

translation.text: 文字系统

source.text: Unlike English, the Japanese language has three distinct writing systems. This lets you spell the same word in multiple ways - sometimes dozens of ways - to achieve different effects. What's more, the Japanese language even allows you to write words on top of other words to achieve various effects not possible in other languages. Unsurprisingly, these effects tend to get flattened in a literal translation.
source.raw:

translation.text: 与英语不同，日语有三套不同的文字系统。同一个词可以有多种写法，有时甚至几十种，能产生不同效果。日语还可以在词语上面再写一层文字，做到其他语言做不到的事。这些效果往往在直译中被磨平，也就不奇怪了。

source.text: Numbers
source.raw: Numbers

translation.text: 数字

source.text: If you type "58008" on a calculator and turn it upside down, it makes English speaking schoolchildren laugh because it spells "BOOBS". This numberplay would make little sense to non-English speakers, however. Similarly, the Japanese language has its own unique forms of numberplay that make zero sense in other languages - November 4•h can be interpreted as "Nice Butt Day", for example. When language is involved, numbers lose their literal predictability.

Japanese language has its own unique forms of numberplay that make zero sense
in other languages - November 4•h can be interpreted as "Nice Butt Day", for
example. When language is involved, numbers lose their literal predictability.

translation.text: 在计算器上输入“58008”，再上下颠倒，会让英语国家的小学生发笑，因为它看起来像“BOOBS”（胸部）。不过，不懂英语的人恐怕不明白这个数字游戏。日语同样有别的语言完全看不懂的数字游戏，例如11月4日可以解作“美臀日”。一旦牵涉语言，数字也不再总能按字面理解。

page.title: 创意的表达形式
page.subtitle: 什么是本地化？ · 私人学习译稿

source.text: Creative Packaging
source.raw: Creative Packaging

translation.text: 创意的表达形式

source.text: Sometimes, it's not the words themselves that are difficult to translate, but how they're presented. Literal translations tend to fall apart when this type of "creative packaging" is involved. Here are a few simple examples.
source.raw:
Sometimes, it's not the words themselves that are difficult to translate, but
how they're presented. Literal translations tend to fall apart when this type of
"creative packaging" is involved. Here are a few simple examples.

translation.text: 有时难译的不是词语本身，而是它们的呈现方式。碰上这种“创意包装”，直译往往会失效。下面是几个简单例子。

source.text: Clues and Hints
source.raw: Clues and Hints

translation.text: 线索与提示

source.text: Writers sometimes include meticulously worded hints meant to guide the reader or lead the reader astray. Such hints might be used as mystery clues, as foreshadowing devices, or to say something indirectly. Naturally, a carefully crafted hint can easily break during translation.
source.raw:
Writers sometimes include meticulously worded hints meant to guide the
reader or lead the reader astray. Such hints might be used as mystery clues, as
foreshadowing devices, or to say something indirectly. Naturally, a carefully
crafted hint can easily break during translation.

translation.text: 作者有时会用精心斟酌的措辞引导读者，或把读者引向歧途。这些提示可以是谜题线索、伏笔，也可以用来委婉表达。这样的精巧安排，自然很容易在翻译中失灵。

source.text: Poetry
source.raw: Poetry

translation.text: 诗歌

source.text: Rhyme, rhythm, and syllable counts are important in poetry, but tend to get lost in a literal translation. For example, a literal translation of a Japanese haiku into English will probably have too many syllables to still be a traditional haiku.
source.raw:
Rhyme, rhythm, and syllable counts are important in poetry, but tend to get lost
in a literal translation. For example, a literal translation of a Japanese haiku
into English will probably have too many syllables to still be a traditional haiku.

translation.text: 押韵、节奏和音节数对诗歌很重要，却往往在直译中丢失。例如，把日语俳句直译成英语，音节通常会多到不再符合传统俳句的形式。

source.text: Songs
source.raw: Songs

translation.text: 歌曲

source.text: Songs present a similar creative packaging problem. A literal translation of "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" into Japanese, for example, will result in lyrics that no longer fit the music. The natural solution, then, is to tweak the translation until they do fit the music:

source.text: Avoiding Side Effects
source.raw: Avoiding Side Effects

translation.text: 避免意外含义

source.text: Sometimes, literal translations simply come across as odd or confusing. Occasionally, they might even carry extra, unintended meanings in the target language. If left as-is, these translations risk conveying something the original creator never intended.
source.raw:
Sometimes, literal translations simply come across as odd or confusing.
Occasionally, they might even carry extra, unintended meanings in the target
language. If left as-is, these translations risk conveying something the original
creator never intended.

translation.text: 有时，直译只是显得古怪或令人困惑；有时却会在目标语言里带出原本没有的意思。若原样保留，就可能传达创作者从未想表达的内容。

source.text: Redundancy
source.raw: Redundancy

translation.text: 重复与多余

source.text: Sometimes a literal translation might sound unintentionally redundant or foolish. This is common in entertainment translation when special terminology is being defined, and said terminology uses words from a foreign language. Redundancy can also occur when a word sounds complicated in the original language but simple in the target language.
source.raw:
Sometimes a literal translation might sound unintentionally redundant or
foolish. This is common in entertainment translation when special terminology
is being defined, and said terminology uses words from a foreign language.
Redundancy can also occur when a word sounds complicated in the original
language but simple in the target language.

translation.text: 有时直译会无意间显得重复或可笑。娱乐作品在解释专门术语、而术语又借用了外语词时，这种情况很常见。一个词在原语言里听着复杂，在目标语言里却很简单，也可能造成重复。

source.text: Sounding Funny or Improper
source.raw: Sounding Funny or Improper

translation.text: 滑稽或不雅

source.text: A literal translation can leave an unintended impression if it sounds funny or inappropriate in the target language. For example, there's an item in the Pokemon series that restores Power Points. In Japanese, the item is literally called the "PP Aid". This name would sound unintentionally funny and inappropriate in English, however, so the item was renamed to something tamer during localization.
source.raw:
A literal translation can leave an unintended impression if it sounds funny
or inappropriate in the target language. For example, there's an item in the
Pokemon series that restores Power Points. In Japanese, the item is literally
called the "PP Aid". This name would sound unintentionally funny and
inappropriate in English, however, so the item was renamed to something
tamer during localization.

translation.text: 直译若在目标语言里听着滑稽或不妥，就会留下意外的印象。例如《Pokémon》系列有一种恢复招式点数的道具，日语名称直译是“PP Aid”（PP辅助剂）。但这个名字在英语里听着意外地滑稽、不雅（PP 与 pee-pee“尿尿”同音），所以本地化时改成了更稳妥的名字。

source.text: Ambiguity
source.raw: Ambiguity

translation.text: 歧义

source.text: A literal translation of an idea that's clearly defined in the source language can become ambiguous in the target language. For example, the Japanese term hikari dameji literally means "light damage" in English. But wait, does that mean "damage that isn't severe" or does it mean "damage from light beams"? In Japanese, it's clearly the latter, but the literal English translation paves the way for confusion.
source.raw:
A literal translation of an idea that's clearly defined in the source language can
become ambiguous in the target language. For example, the Japanese term
hikari dameji literally means "light damage" in English. But wait, does that
mean "damage that isn't severe" or does it mean "damage from light beams"?
In Japanese, it's clearly the latter, but the literal English translation paves the
way for confusion.

translation.text: 原语言里清楚明确的概念，直译后可能产生歧义。例如日语 hikari damēji（光属性伤害），直译成英语是 light damage。但等等：是“轻微伤害”，还是“光束造成的伤害”？日语明确是后者，英语直译却给误解留下了空间。

page.title: 外部因素
page.subtitle: 什么是本地化？ · 私人学习译稿

source.text: External Influences
source.raw: External Influences

translation.text: 外部因素

source.text: Being a professional translator is a lot like being a professional chef- a customer hires you to create something that needs to follow custom specifications. For example, a restaurant customer can order a hamburger, but ask that it be cooked a certain way and include specific toppings. Similarly, a translation client can order something to be translated according to their custom requirements, like "each line of text can only be 22 letters long" or "use these specific terms in these situations".
source.raw:
Being a professional translator is a lot like being a professional chef- a customer
hires you to create something that needs to follow custom specifications.
For example, a restaurant customer can order a hamburger, but ask that it be
cooked a certain way and include specific toppings. Similarly, a translation
client can order something to be translated according to their custom
requirements, like "each line of text can only be 22 letters long" or "use these
specific terms in these situations".

translation.text: 职业译者很像职业厨师：客户雇你制作符合具体要求的东西。例如，餐厅顾客可以点汉堡，同时指定做法和配料。翻译客户也可以要求按自己的规定来译，比如“每行只能有22个字母”，或“在这些情形下使用指定术语”。

source.text: What's more, customers are also free to modify the final product as they see fit. If a restaurant customer wants to set their hamburger on fire or turn it into a horrifying birthday cake, they can do that. Likewise, a translation client can edit the final product however they want. Basically, clients have direct influence over how a translation is performed and how it's ultimately presented.
source.raw:
What's more, customers are also free to modify the final product as they
see fit. If a restaurant customer wants to set their hamburger on fire or turn
it into a horrifying birthday cake, they can do that. Likewise, a translation
client can edit the final product however they want. Basically, clients have
direct influence over how a translation is performed and how it's ultimately
presented.

translation.text: 而且，顾客可以随意改动成品。餐厅顾客想把汉堡点着，或把它变成恐怖的生日蛋糕，都是他的自由。翻译客户也一样，可以随意编辑交付稿。客户能直接影响翻译如何进行，以及最后如何呈现。

source.text: When it comes to entertainment translation, clients are one part of the equation, but there are other parts too. The original creator, for example, might demand that certain names be spelled certain ways, or that certain terms be translated in certain ways. Industry and corporate guidelines might also demand that certain things be handled in certain ways. And, of course, local laws and cultural values can have an effect on the final product.
source.raw:
When it comes to entertainment translation, clients are one part of the
equation, but there are other parts too. The original creator, for example, might
demand that certain names be spelled certain ways, or that certain terms
be translated in certain ways. Industry and corporate guidelines might also
demand that certain things be handled in certain ways. And, of course, local
laws and cultural values can have an effect on the final product.

translation.text: 在娱乐作品翻译中，客户只是影响因素之一。原作者可能要求某些名字按指定方式拼写，某些词按指定方式翻译。行业准则、公司规定也可能要求按特定方式处理内容。当然，当地法律和文化价值观同样会影响成品。

source.text: These changes were especially common in video game localizations during the 1990s and 2000s. However, as the times change, the external influences on the localization process can change too.

translation.text: 这些改动在20世纪90年代和21世纪头十年的游戏本地化中尤其常见。不过，时代变了，影响本地化的外部因素也会变化。

source.text: In short, professional entertainment localization rarely happens in a vacuum - there are almost always external factors that might cause something to deviate from a straightforward, literal translation.
source.raw:
In short, professional entertainment localization rarely happens in a vacuum -
there are almost always external factors that might cause something to deviate
from a straightforward, literal translation.

translation.text: 总之，职业娱乐本地化很少独立进行：几乎总有外部因素，可能让译文偏离直接的字面翻译。

source.text: "The translated script MUST be half the length of the original text, oh, and after you're done we'll insert some memes!"

MUST be half the

translation.text: “译稿长度必须只有原文的一半！哦，对了，你译完我们还要塞几个梗进去！”

source.text: It's common to see jokes, references, and text changes added to translated games. When such added content is unwarranted, it technically ceases to be a translation or a localization. Because the result no longer reflects the original's intention, it becomes more of a "transformation" or "alteration". I'm not fond of this practice myself, and as a professional translator I don't feel comfortable tinkering with others' creativity.
source.raw:
It's common to see jokes, references, and text changes added to translated
games. When such added content is unwarranted, it technically ceases to
be a translation or a localization. Because the result no longer reflects the
original's intention, it becomes more of a "transformation" or "alteration".
I'm not fond of this practice myself, and as a professional translator I don't
feel comfortable tinkering with others' creativity.

translation.text: 游戏译版里常会新增笑话、典故或文字改动。如果这种添加没有正当理由，严格来说就不再是翻译或本地化了。结果不再体现原作意图，更像是“变形”或“改造”。我个人不喜欢这样做；作为职业译者，随意摆弄别人的创作，也让我不自在。

page.subtitle: 什么是本地化？ · 私人学习译稿

source.text: Unpredictable Circumstances
source.raw: Unpredictable Circumstances

translation.text: 无法预知的情况

source.text: Sometimes, the lack of external information can cause a literal translation to fail later on. This is common when translating ongoing entertainment series. In these situations, it's possible that only the original creator knows where the story will go. Or it's possible that the creator has no idea and is making things up as they go. Either way, without input from the creator, a translator can only hope and guess which insignificant things will become significant later on.
source.raw:
Sometimes, the lack of external information can cause a literal translation to
fail later on. This is common when translating ongoing entertainment series.
In these situations, it's possible that only the original creator knows where the
story will go. Or it's possible that the creator has no idea and is making things
up as they go. Either way, without input from the creator, a translator can only
hope and guess which insignificant things will become significant later on.

translation.text: 有时缺乏外部信息，会让当时的直译在日后出错。翻译仍在连载的娱乐作品时，这很常见：可能只有原作者知道故事将走向哪里，也可能作者自己并不知道，正边写边想。无论哪种情况，没有作者提供信息，译者只能猜测哪些看似无关紧要的细节会在以后变得重要，并希望自己猜中。

source.text: As an example, an important island in the One Piece series named ラフテル (rafuteru) was introduced in 1999. Because the Japanese language doesn’t distinguish between “L” and “R” sounds, and because the series’ creator wasn’t involved in the translation process, English translators originally called the island “Raftel”, hoping this literal transcription was correct. In 2019, with the series still chugging along, it was finally revealed that the creator intended the name to be “Laugh Tale” all along.
source.raw:
As an example, an important island in the One Piece series named 777-Jv
(rafuteru) was introduced in 1999. Because the Japanese language doesn't
distinguish between "L" and "R" sounds, and because the series' creator wasn't
involved in the translation process, English translators originally called the
island "Raftel", hoping this literal transcription was correct. In 2019, with the
series still chugging along, it was finally revealed that the creator intended the
name to be "Laugh Tale" all along.

translation.text: 例如，《One Piece》在1999年提到一座重要的岛，名叫ラフテル（rafuteru）。日语不区分 L 和 R 的发音，而原作者没有参与翻译，英语译者便先将岛名拼成 Raftel，希望这种直接音译是对的。到2019年，故事仍在连载，大家才终于得知：作者从一开始想的就是 Laugh Tale（笑谈）。

source.text: All Together
source.raw: All Together

translation.text: 合起来看

source.text: As we've seen in this chapter, a lot can get lost in translation if you only focus on the words used. Recognizing and preserving the ideas behind those words is arguably more important, and is at the heart of what localization is all about.
source.raw:
As we've seen in this chapter, a lot can get lost in translation if you only focus
on the words used. Recognizing and preserving the ideas behind those words is
arguably more important, and is at the heart of what localization is all about.

translation.text: 本章说明，只盯着词语本身，翻译就可能丢掉很多东西。认清并保留词语背后的想法，或许更为重要；这也正是本地化的核心。

source.text: In this third Legends of Localization book, we'll look at the specific things that changed during Undertale's translation process into Japanese. And given that the game relies so much on humor, unique speech patterns, cultural references, and more, there'll surely be a lot to discover!
source.raw:
In this third Legends ofL ocalization book, we'll look at the specific things that
changed during Underta/e's translation process into Japanese. And given that
the game relies so much on humor, unique speech patterns, cultural references,
and more, there'll surely be a lot to discover!

translation.text: 在《Legends of Localization》第3卷中，我们将具体看看 Undertale 译成日语时改动了什么。游戏大量依靠幽默、独特的说话方式、文化典故等元素，一定有不少值得发现的内容！

source.text: Game Overview
source.raw: Game Overview

translation.text: 游戏概况

source.text: Undertale is a popular, award-winning video game that debuted in 2015. It was created and developed largely by one person: Toby Fox.
source.raw:
Underta/e is a popular, award-winning video game that debuted in 2015. It was
created and developed largely by one person: Toby Fox.

translation.text: Undertale 是一款广受欢迎、屡获奖项的游戏，2015年首次推出，创作和开发工作大多由 Toby Fox 一人完成。

source.text: At first glance, Undertale doesn't seem particularly impressive - it has simple graphics, a strange battle system, and looks more like a fun little hobby project than a serious game. But first impressions can be deceiving: Undertale actually combines different game genres to create something fresh, sabotages veteran gamers' expectations about how games should work, and builds upon the foundation laid by previous generations of game creators.
source.raw:
At first glance, Undertale doesn't seem particularly impressive - it has simple
graphics, a strange battle system, and looks more like a fun little hobby project
than a serious game. But first impressions can be deceiving: Undertale actually
combines different game genres to create something fresh, sabotages veteran
gamers' expectations about how games should work, and builds upon the
foundation laid by previous generations of game creators.

translation.text: 乍看之下，Undertale 似乎并不惊艳：画面简单，战斗系统古怪，更像一个有趣的业余小项目，而非正经大作。但第一印象会骗人。它融合了不同游戏类型，创造出新鲜体验，打破老玩家对游戏运作方式的预期，也建立在前几代游戏创作者打下的基础上。

source.text: At its core, for example, Undertale combines the gameplay of a classic Japanese role-playing game with the mechanics of "bullet hell" shoot-em-up games. This unique combination surprised gamers when Undertale debuted.
source.raw:
At its core, for example, Undertale combines the gameplay of a classic Japanese
role-playing game with the mechanics of "bullet hell" shoot-em-up games.
This unique combination surprised gamers when Undertale debuted.

source.text: Morality
source.raw: Morality

translation.text: 道德选择

source.text: When you think about it, many video games basically boil down to "you beat up and/or kill the bad guys". It's almost the expected "default" of any game. This was true for beloved classics like Pac-Man, Space Invaders, and Super Mario Bros., and it's just as true for games released today.
source.raw:
When you think about it, many video games basically boil down to "you beat up
and/or kill the bad guys". It's almost the expected "default" of any game. This
was true for beloved classics like Pac-Man, Space Invaders, and Super Mario
Bros., and it's just as true for games released today.

translation.text: 仔细想想，很多游戏归根到底都是“打倒或杀死坏人”。这几乎成了玩家默认的游戏规则。备受喜爱的《Pac-Man》《Space Invaders》和《Super Mario Bros.》等经典如此，今天的新游戏也一样。

source.text: Undertale looks at things differently. Instead of hurting enemies, you can talk to them, flatter them, insult them, comfort them, mock them, befriend them, and more, until they lose the will to fight. In short, you can complete the game without killing anything or anyone. Or, if you want, you can slaughter everything you see - the choice is up to you. The game also changes with each choice you make, ensuring that no two Undertale experiences are exactly the same.
source.raw:
Undertale looks at things differently. Instead of hurting enemies, you can talk
to them, flatter them, insult them, comfort them, mock them, befriend them,
and more, until they lose the will to fight. In short, you can complete the game
without killing anything or anyone. Or, if you want, you can slaughter everything
you see - the choice is up to you. The game also changes with each choice you
make, ensuring that no two Undertale experiences are exactly the same.

translation.text: Undertale 换了个角度。你不必伤害敌人，可以与他们交谈、奉承、辱骂、安慰、嘲弄，或交朋友，直到他们不再想打。你可以不杀任何东西、任何人就通关；也可以随心所欲地杀光眼前的一切，选择在你。游戏还会随每次选择发生变化，没有两段 Undertale 体验会完全一样。

source.text: What kind of person are you, deep down? Undertale will show you.
source.raw: What kind of person are you, deep down? Undertale will show you.

translation.text: 你的内心究竟是怎样的人？Undertale 会让你看见。

source.text: Nintendo encourages players to literally kill enemies in Super Mario Bros.
source.raw:
Nintendo encourages
players to literally
kill enemies in Super
Mario Bros.

translation.text: 任天堂在《Super Mario Bros.》中，确实鼓励玩家杀死敌人。

source.text: Undertale follows the standard Japanese RPG formula of exploring, talking, and fighting, but every aspect of the game has a surprising amount of charm and polish to it
source.raw:
Underta/e follows the standard Japanese RPG
formula of exploring, talking, and fighting,
but every aspect of the game has a surprising
amount of charm and polish to it

translation.text: Undertale 沿用了日式角色扮演游戏中探索、交谈、战斗的基本框架，却在每个方面都打磨得细致而迷人。

source.text: Every enemy in Undertale has a uniquely themed "bullet hell" pattern that the player must react to in battle
source.raw:
Every enemy in Underta/e has a uniquely
themed "bullet hell" pattern that the player
must react to in battle

translation.text: Undertale 的每种敌人都有独特主题的“弹幕”，玩家必须在战斗中作出反应。

source.text: Enemies in Undertale are actual characters in the game with feelings and motivations of their own. You can treat them like standard video game battle fodder, or you can let them live and befriend them. The choice you make each time will change the game in big and small ways!
source.raw:
Enemies in Underta/e are actual characters in the game with feelings and motivations of their
own. You can treat them like standard video game battle fodder, or you can let them live and
befriend them. The choice you make each time will change the game in big and small ways!

translation.text: Undertale 的敌人是有感情、有动机的角色。你可以把他们当成普通游戏里的战斗炮灰，也可以放他们活着，与他们交朋友。每一次选择都会或大或小地改变游戏！

source.text: Who you are really does seem to impact your Undertale experience. Impatient players tend to rush through, kill everything, and skip all the text. Cautious players stop to analyze every choice. Judgmental players begin with an already unswayable opinion. Timid players constantly worry about upsetting enemies in battle. It's an interesting phenomenon to see!
source.raw:
Who you are really does seem to impact your Undertale experience.
Impatient players tend to rush through, kill everything, and skip all the
text. Cautious players stop to analyze every choice. Judgmental players
begin with an already unswayable opinion. Timid players constantly worry
about upsetting enemies in battle. It's an interesting phenomenon to see!

translation.text: 你是怎样的人，似乎真会影响 Undertale 的体验。急性子往往一路冲，见谁杀谁，跳过所有文字；谨慎的人停下来分析每个选择；爱下判断的人还没开始，就已有不可动摇的看法；胆小的人则总担心在战斗中惹敌人生气。这个现象很有意思！

source.text: The Man Behind the Game
source.raw: The Man Behind the Game

translation.text: 游戏背后的那个人

source.text: Whether they want it or not, many successful authors, musicians, directors, and celebrities stand atop a pedestal of fame that puts them out of reach of the ordinary person. To some degree, this applies to video game creators, too.
source.raw:
Whether they want it or not, many successful authors, musicians, directors,
and celebrities stand atop a pedestal of fame that puts them out of reach of the
ordinary person. To some degree, this applies to video game creators, too.

translation.text: 许多成功的作家、音乐人、导演和名人，无论愿不愿意，都被名气抬到了普通人难以接近的位置。游戏创作者在某种程度上也一样。

source.text: Toby Fox, the developer of Undertale, is the opposite: despite his fame, he's literally just an ordinary guy from the Internet who makes weird jokes and hangs out online. Here is his story.
source.raw:
Toby Fox, the developer of Undertale, is the opposite: despite his fame, he's
literally just an ordinary guy from the Internet who makes weird jokes and
hangs out online. Here is his story.

translation.text: Undertale 的开发者 Toby Fox 却相反：虽然出名，他确实就是个普通网友，上网闲逛，说些怪笑话。下面是他的故事。
20世纪90年代：

source.text: Toby grows up playing popular video games that are considered classics today. He's especially fond of Japanese role-playing games that have been translated into English. These games feature memorable stories, characters, and music.

source.text: Of course, it's not accurate to say that Toby created Undertale entirely by himself. He received lots of help from friends and supporters during the game's development - everything from art to character design to fashion tips, and more. Although Toby did create the vast majority of the game, it would be unfair to discount the work of everyone else who contributed. Without their contributions, Undertale would be a noticeably different game today.

source.text: Toby joins a community for fans of Homestuck, a popular multimedia comic series. For fun, he remixes Homes tuck music and shares it with other fans. The series creators, impressed by Toby's work, bring him on as an official music producer in 2010. Despite being entirely self-taught, Toby quickly becomes a revered musician in the Homestuck community. As a hobby, Toby also begins to design a video game that will eventually be known as Undertale.

page.title: 制作 Undertale
page.subtitle: 历史 · 私人学习译稿

source.text: After receiving his university degree, Toby continues to compose music for Homes tuck and design games for fun. During this time, he uses another game creation tool known known as Game Maker to continue developing Undertale.
source.raw:
After receiving his university degree, Toby continues to compose music for
Homes tuck and design games for fun. During this time, he uses another game
creation tool known known as Game Maker to continue developing Undertale.

translation.text: 大学毕业后，Toby 继续为 Homestuck 作曲，也继续把设计游戏当作爱好。这期间，他改用另一款游戏制作工具 Game Maker，继续开发 Undertale。

source.text: Eventually, Toby releases a short, playable demo of Undertale to the public. The positive response encourages him to launch a crowdfunding campaign to fund further development. The campaign is a success, and allows Toby to spend the next two years developing the Undertale demo into a full-length game.
source.raw:
Eventually, Toby releases a short, playable demo of Undertale to the public. The
positive response encourages him to launch a crowdfunding campaign to fund
further development. The campaign is a success, and allows Toby to spend the
next two years developing the Undertale demo into a full-length game.

translation.text: 后来，Toby 向公众发布了一段可玩的 Undertale 演示版。良好反馈鼓励他发起众筹，为后续开发筹钱。众筹成功了，让他得以用接下来的两年，将演示版扩展成完整游戏。

source.text: In 2015, Toby releases his full, finished version of Undertale. The once-na'ive RPG Maker kid is now a professional game developer.
source.raw:

translation.text: 2015年，Toby 发布了制作完成的 Undertale。曾经那个懵懂的 RPG Maker 少年，如今已是职业游戏开发者。

source.text: If you do any updates to the game, I might make it so NPCs can't walk through you. Also, a button to make the text scroll twice as fast (or instantly jump the ending position of the string) would be REALLY appreciated. instantly jump the ending position of the string) would be REALLY

source.text: Release
source.raw: Release

translation.text: 发行

source.text: Undertale debuted on September 15, 2015, in English only, and only for home computers. Toby had wanted to release the game on mainstream game consoles too, but the Game Maker program he used to create Undertale didn't suitably support the newest consoles at the time.
source.raw:
Undertale debuted on September 15, 2015, in English only, and only for home
computers. Toby had wanted to release the game on mainstream game
consoles too, but the Game Maker program he used to create Undertale didn't
suitably support the newest consoles at the time.

translation.text: Undertale 于2015年9月15日首次发行，只有英语版，也只登陆个人电脑。Toby 原本还想登陆主流游戏主机，但当时用来制作游戏的 Game Maker，无法充分支持最新主机。

source.text: In 2016, Toby teamed up with the Japanese company 8-4, Ltd. to localize his computer game into Japanese. During the localization process, 8-4 offered to perform the additional technical work needed to release Undertale on game consoles as well. The shared hope was that a console release could make Undertale accessible to a wider audience in Japan, where computer gaming was relatively niche.
source.raw:
In 2016, Toby teamed up with the Japanese company 8-4, Ltd. to localize his
computer game into Japanese. During the localization process, 8-4 offered to
perform the additional technical work needed to release Underta/e on game
consoles as well. The shared hope was that a console release could make
Undertale accessible to a wider audience in Japan, where computer gaming
was relatively niche.

translation.text: 2016年，Toby 与日本公司 8-4, Ltd. 合作，将电脑版游戏本地化为日语。过程中，8-4 提出承担额外的技术工作，让 Undertale 也能在主机发行。双方希望，主机版能在电脑游戏相对小众的日本触达更多玩家。

source.text: Over the next several years, Toby and 8-4 released Undertale for Japanese computers and a variety of game consoles, including the PlayStation 4, the PlayStation Vita, the Nintendo Switch, and the Xbox One. Each port included new and exclusive content, along with the option to switch the game's text between English and Japanese at any time.
source.raw:
Over the next several years, Toby and 8-4 released Undertale for Japanese
computers and a variety of game consoles, including the PlayStation 4, the
PlayStation Vita, the Nintendo Switch, and the Xbox One. Each port included
new and exclusive content, along with the option to switch the game's text
between English and Japanese at any time.

translation.text: 随后几年，Toby 和 8-4 推出了日语电脑版，以及 PlayStation 4、PlayStation Vita、Nintendo Switch、Xbox One 等主机版本。每个移植版都有新增的独占内容，并可随时在英语和日语文本之间切换。

translation.text: 反响

source.text: After its release in 2015, Undertale enjoyed major success in almost every way.
source.raw: After its release in 2015, Undertale enjoyed major success in almost every way.

translation.text: 2015年发行后，Undertale 几乎在各方面都大获成功。

source.text: Sales-wise, Undertale was a clear success. Through word of mouth, the game sold over 500,000 copies in its first three months. That number has since reached into the millions - a level usually only achieved by industry titans like Nintendo and Sony.
source.raw:
Sales-wise, Undertale was a clear success. Through word of mouth, the game
sold over 500,000 copies in its first three months. That number has since
reached into the millions - a level usually only achieved by industry titans like
Nintendo and Sony.

translation.text: 销量上，它无疑取得了成功。靠玩家口口相传，前三个月就售出超过50万份；后来更达到数百万份，通常只有任天堂、索尼这样的业界巨头才做得到。

source.text: Undertale also achieved critical success - the game received acclaim from game critics, reviewers, and industry veterans alike. News of Undertale's success even reached mainstream outlets, which led to further recognition outside gaming circles.
source.raw:
Undertale also achieved critical success - the game received acclaim from game
critics, reviewers, and industry veterans alike. News of Undertale's success
even reached mainstream outlets, which led to further recognition outside
gaming circles.

translation.text: 口碑也同样出色：游戏评论家、评测者和业界资深人士纷纷称赞。成功的消息甚至传进主流媒体，让游戏圈以外也有更多人认识了它。

source.text: '' It was a whispered reminder that great games can do more than impress with sheer complexity and breadth, they can also draw us in close to them as to engage with our humanity." - GIANT BOMB

'' It was a whispered reminder that great games can do more than impress

translation.text: “它像一声低语，提醒我们：优秀游戏不只靠复杂与庞大令人惊叹，也能让我们亲近它，触动我们的人性。”——GIANT BOMB

source.text: '' Undertale is a post-modern masterpiece. Toby Fox, its creator, has produced a work of interactive narrative art that is moving, surreal - and fiendishly clever." - THE NATIONAL
source.raw:

source.text: '' Toby Fox,forces us[. . ) to really think about why we do the things we do in games by utilizing a mix of humor, regret, and relationships to form one of the most important game releases of2 015." -VENTURE BEAT

source.text: Undertale was also a hit with players. A massive fan following grew overnight. Undertale costumes were suddenly everywhere. Undertale concerts with full symphony orchestras were held around the world. Countless Undertale fan games and Undertale-inspired games were shared online. Even sketchy bootleg companies began pumping out every type of poor quality Undertale merchandise imaginable.
source.raw:
Undertale was also a hit with players. A massive fan following grew overnight.
Undertale costumes were suddenly everywhere. Undertale concerts with
full symphony orchestras were held around the world. Countless Undertale
fan games and Underta/e-inspired games were shared online. Even sketchy
bootleg companies began pumping out every type of poor quality Undertale
merchandise imaginable.

translation.text: 玩家也爱上了 Undertale。庞大的爱好者群体一夜间形成，角色扮演服装突然随处可见；完整交响乐团演奏的音乐会在世界各地举办；无数同人游戏、受其启发的游戏出现在网上。连可疑的盗版商家都开始大量制造各种想得到的劣质 Undertale 周边。

source.text: At the same time, fans around the world clamored to play Undertale in their native languages. Before long, fans translated the game into over a dozen languages. These unofficial translations helped non-English speakers experience the game, which led to further recognition and success.
source.raw:
At the same time, fans around the world clamored to play Undertale in
their native languages. Before long, fans translated the game into over a
dozen languages. These unofficial translations helped non-English speakers

translation.text: 与此同时，世界各地的玩家纷纷希望用母语游玩。不久，玩家就将游戏译成了十几种语言。这些非官方译版让不懂英语的人也能体验游戏，进一步带来关注与成功。

source.text: In short, Undertale was a big deal for many people: fans, critics, the game industry, and, of course, Toby himself.
source.raw:
In short, Undertale was a big deal for many people: fans, critics, the game

translation.text: 总之，对玩家、评论者、游戏业界，当然还有 Toby 本人而言，Undertale 都是一件大事。

source.text: Japanese Releases

translation.text: 日本的发行历程

source.text: When Undertale debuted in English in September 2015, it wasn't locked to a single region - gamers anywhere in the world could purchase it. The game was only available in English, however, and could only be played on home computers. This language barrier, coupled with the need for a computer, made the gam inaccessible for most Japanese gamers. As a result, Undertale experienced a very different "release history" in Japan that can be divided into three distinct stages.
source.raw:
When Under tale debuted in English in September 2015, it wasn't locked to a
single region - gamers anywhere in the world could purchase it. The game was
only available in English, however, and could only be played on home computers.
This language barrier, coupled with the need for a computer, made the gam
inaccessible for most Japanese gamers. As a result, Undertale experienced a very
different "release history" in Japan that can be divided into three distinct stages.

translation.text: 2015年9月，Undertale 英语版首次推出时没有锁区，世界各地的玩家都能购买。不过，游戏只有英语，也只能在个人电脑上运行。语言障碍加上电脑要求，让多数日本玩家难以接触它。因此，Undertale 在日本经历了一段很不同的“发行史”，大致可分成三个阶段。

source.text: Stage #1: Videos
source.raw: Stage #1: Videos

translation.text: 第一阶段：视频

source.text: In October 2015, several weeks after Undertale's English release, a Japanese gamer began to upload a series of Undertale gameplay videos to NicoNico Douga, a popular Japanese video site. These videos, which were painstakingly edited to include Japanese translations of all the English text, quickly gained impressive view counts.

source.text: Because these early Undertale translations were presented as online videos, viewers could use the comment sections to react to the game as a community and to point out translation problems. Although these early video translations helped foster awareness and appreciation for Undertale in Japan, the game remained a small, niche secret until early 2016.

source.text: Stage #2: Fan Translation

translation.text: 第二阶段：民间翻译

source.text: In March 2016, fans released an unofficial translation "patch" that could replace all of the original English text in the game with translated Japanese text. At last, Japanese gamers could play Undertale for themselves in their native language. The fan community quickly exploded in size, and videos of the fan translation spread awareness of the game even further.

source.text: Although this unofficial translation made the game playable in Japanese, other barriers stood in the way. First, the vast majority of Japanese gamers at the time relied on mainstream gaming systems or mobile devices to play games, not home computers. Players would also need to be savvy enough to buy the original game from English-language websites, download the translation patch from elsewhere, decompress the files, apply the patch successfully, and deal with any technical issues along the way. Thus Undertale remained inaccessible to most Japanese gamers.

page.title: 不同译版之间的争论
page.subtitle: 历史 · 私人学习译稿

source.text: Criticism of Competing Translations
source.raw: Criticism of Competing Translations

translation.text: 不同译版之间的争论

source.text: Whenever something receives multiple translations, an interesting psychological phenomenon takes shape: people tend to unconsciously cling to the very first translation they encounter, and compare all other translations against it. I call this phenomenon "imprinting", based on a psychological term that refers to bow newborn animals naturally bond to the first things they learn to recognize.
source.raw:
Whenever something receives multiple translations, an interesting
psychological phenomenon takes shape: people tend to unconsciously
cling to the very first translation they encounter, and compare all other
translations against it. I call this phenomenon "imprinting", based on a
psychological term that refers to bow newborn animals naturally bond to the
first things they learn to recognize.

translation.text: 只要同一作品有多个译版，就会出现一种有趣的心理现象：人们往往不自觉地依恋最先接触的译版，并拿它衡量其他版本。我借用心理学术语，将这种现象称为“印随”，这个词原指新生动物自然依附于最先学会辨认的对象。

source.text: In translation, this imprinting phenomenon often leads to an excessive, irrational attachment to the first translation you encounter, regardless of the translation's quality or genuine flaws. Imprinting isn't limited to translation, of course, and can potentially occur with any sort of first experience.
source.raw:
In translation, this imprinting phenomenon often leads to an excessive,
irrational attachment to the first translation you encounter, regardless of the
translation's quality or genuine flaws. Imprinting isn't limited to translation, of
course, and can potentially occur with any sort of first experience.

translation.text: 翻译中的印随现象，常让人不顾译文质量和实际缺点，过度、非理性地依恋最先见到的版本。当然，印随不局限于翻译，任何首次体验都有可能如此。

source.text: Undertale's official Japanese release caused two general groups to form: fans who first experienced the fan translations, and fans who first experienced the official translation.
source.raw:
Underta/e's official Japanese release caused two general groups to form: fans
who first experienced the fan translations, and fans who first experienced the
official translation.

translation.text: Undertale 官方日语版问世后，大致形成两群玩家：先接触民间译版的人，以及先接触官方译版的人。

source.text: Naturally, some imprinted fan-translation players were quick to criticize the new translation. Just the announcement of an official Japanese release prompted these fans to use phrases like "war criminals", "unfaithful", and "pointless".
source.raw:
Naturally, some imprinted fan-translation players were quick to criticize the new
translation. Just the announcement of an official Japanese release prompted
these fans to use phrases like "war criminals", "unfaithful", and "pointless".

translation.text: 一些受印随影响的民间译版玩家，自然很快就开始批评新译版。甚至只公布官方日语版的消息，就有人用上“战犯”“不忠于原作”“毫无意义”这样的字眼。

source.text: Conversely, some fans who played the official translation first were quick to criticize the unofficial fan translations. These newer fans described the unofficial translations with phrases like "brain damage", "cheesy", and "trying too hard".
source.raw:
Conversely, some fans who played the official translation first were quick to
criticize the unofficial fan translations. These newer fans described the unofficial
translations with phrases like "brain damage", "cheesy", and "trying too hard".

translation.text: 反过来，一些先玩官方译版的人，也很快开始批评民间译版。他们用“脑残”“俗气”“用力过猛”等词来形容非官方翻译。

source.text: Interestingly, a third group of fans responded to the official release with comments like "a true fan will play both then interpret stuff however they want" and "the official and unofficial translation factions are already waging war, I think I'm gonna get some popcorn and beer and laugh my ass off".
source.raw:
Interestingly, a third group of fans responded to the official release with
comments like "a true fan will play both then interpret stuff however they

translation.text: 有趣的是，第三群玩家这样回应官方版：“真粉丝会两版都玩，再按自己的意思理解”，或“官方派和民间派已经打起来了，我要拿点爆米花和啤酒，笑个痛快”。

source.text: It's important to note that this fiery translation debate only took place within a small, loud segment of the fandom. Over time, these arguments cooled down as the official translation took hold. Today, the fan-made translations remain well regarded and serve as examples of the Japanese community's spirit.
source.raw:
It's important to note that this fiery translation debate only took place within a
small, loud segment of the fandom. Over time, these arguments cooled down as
the official translation took hold. Today, the fan-made translations remain well

source.text: Getting it Localized

translation.text: 让游戏走向本地化

source.text: Before Undertale’s English release, Toby told me that he intended to release the game in Japanese sometime. He faced some big questions, though. How do you get a game translated and localized? And how do you ensure the final product is good if you don’t even know the language yourself?

translation.text: 在 Undertale 英文版发售之前，Toby 告诉我，他打算日后推出日文版。不过，他面临着几个大问题：该怎样找人翻译并完成游戏的本地化？如果自己连那门语言都不懂，又该如何确保最终成品的质量？

source.text: In this chapter, we’ll briefly look at how game developers approach localization, who Toby hired to localize Undertale, and how Undertale’s localization process worked on the inside.

translation.text: 本章将简要介绍游戏开发者如何开展本地化、Toby 聘请了谁来为 Undertale 做本地化，以及这个过程在团队内部是如何运作的。

source.text: Who to Turn to

translation.text: 该找谁帮忙

source.text: Let’s say you’re just like Toby and have finished developing your own game. It’s entirely in English, but you’d like to release it in Japan and other countries too. Where do you even start?

translation.text: 假设你和 Toby 一样，刚刚完成自己的游戏。游戏完全是英文的，但你也想在日本和其他国家发行。该从哪里开始呢？

source.text: The answer is pretty simple: translation and localization are no different from any other professional service, like plumbing, computer repair, or accounting. If you’re a big company, chances are you already have in-house staff members – or possibly an entire department – dedicated to handling such matters. Alternatively, you might already have contracts with outside agencies who can handle everything for you.

translation.text: 答案很简单：翻译和本地化与水管维修、电脑维修、会计等专业服务并没有什么不同。如果你是一家大公司，很可能已经有内部员工，甚至整个部门，专门处理这类事务。或者，你可能已经与外部机构签有合同，可以将相关工作全部交给他们。

source.text: But if you’re a small company, or just a single person, you’ll need to seek outside help. In this situation, your first thought might be, “Do I personally know anyone who can do this for me?” If the answer is no, then you might ask around for recommendations instead. And if that yields no leads, then there’s usually only one choice left: find someone on the Internet.

translation.text: 但如果你是一家小公司，或者只有一个人，就需要寻求外部帮助。这时，你首先可能会想：“我认识的人里，有谁能帮我做这件事吗？”如果没有，就可以向周围的人打听推荐。如果仍无线索，通常就只剩下一条路：上网找人。

source.text: As a huge video game company, Nintendo has a dedicated department for localization

translation.text: 任天堂是一家大型游戏公司，设有专门的本地化部门。

source.text: “Bob Johnson” the single developer doesn’t have a dedicated localization department

translation.text: “Bob Johnson”这位独立开发者没有专门的本地化部门。

blocks.notes: 照片中的名字及文字不覆盖；此处只翻译书中图注。

source.text: Unfortunately, searching for “hire a translator” or “hire a localizer” online will result in an avalanche of ads, sites, and companies begging for your business. Many of these services will offer to translate business documents, medical patents, video games, underwear packaging, and everything else you can think of.

translation.text: 然而，在网上搜索“聘请译者”或“聘请本地化人员”，会迎来铺天盖地的广告、网站和招揽生意的公司。这些服务商中，许多都声称可以翻译商务文件、医疗专利、电子游戏、内衣包装，以及你能想到的其他各种内容。

source.text: So, with a million different companies claiming to be experts at every type of translation and localization, how do you know who to pick? In Undertale’s case, Toby experienced it all: he asked friends, he looked around online, and he even received unsolicited offers from companies with in-house localization teams.

translation.text: 面对无数自称精通各种翻译和本地化业务的公司，该怎么选呢？在 Undertale 的案例中，Toby 把这些途径都试过了：向朋友打听、上网寻找，甚至还有设有内部本地化团队的公司主动找上门来。

source.text: Team Building

translation.text: 组建团队

source.text: Not all localization projects are the same - a massive, big-budget game might call for a large team of translators and editors with specialized skill sets, while a small indie game might only warrant a single person juggling multiple responsibi Ii ties.
source.raw:
Not all localization projects are the same - a massive, big-budget game might
call for a large team of translators and editors with specialized skill sets, while
a small indie game might only warrant a single person juggling multiple
responsibi Ii ties.

translation.text: 本地化项目各不相同：大型高预算游戏可能需要很多各有专长的译者和编辑；小型独立游戏则可能只需一人身兼数职。

source.text: In-house localization departments and industry-specific localization companies usually have more resources at their disposal than generic "one stop shop" translation agencies. These extra resources allow for larger localization teams filled with qualified specialists. This means that 8-4, as a dedicated game localization company, was able to give Undertale the same treatment as a big-budget game from a major studio.

In-house localization departments and industry-specific localization

dedicated game localization company, was able to give Undertale the same
treatment as a big-budget game from a major studio.

translation.text: 公司内部的本地化部门、专注某个行业的本地化公司，通常比普通“一站式”翻译机构拥有更多资源，能组建更大的团队，配齐合格的专业人员。因此，作为专门的游戏本地化公司，8-4 能让 Undertale 享受到大型工作室高预算游戏的待遇。

source.text: Slow and Steady
source.raw: Slow and Steady

translation.text: 慢工出细活

source.text: Normally, the complexity of Undertale's script might've warranted two English-to-Japanese translators in order to achieve a timely release. Instead, 8-4 opted to take it slow and only go with one. This meant the game would take longer and cost more money to localize, but it also brought benefits with it:
