translation.text: 右：“Taterus”比“Pop”更早被改回原名，但曾有一小段时间，这两个新名字同时出现在日文剧本中。

source.text: Because Papyrus' text uses the Papyrus font in the English version of Undertale, the localization team considered giving Papyrus a new name to match his new Japanese vertical text. Thus, for only a few weeks during the game's localization, Papyrus was known as "Taterus" - a combination of the Japanese word tate ("vertical") and "Papyrus". This name didn't last long, however, because it sounded too forced and not very funny.
source.raw:
Because Papyrus' text uses the Papyrus font in the English version of Undertale,
the localization team considered giving Papyrus a new name to match his
new Japanese vertical text. Thus, for only a few weeks during the game's
localization, Papyrus was known as "Taterus" - a combination of the Japanese
word tate ("vertical") and "Papyrus". This name didn't last long, however,
because it sounded too forced and not very funny.

translation.text: 由于英语版 Undertale 中 Papyrus 使用 Papyrus 字体，本地化团队考虑给他起个新名字，来配合日文的竖排台词。于是，在本地化过程中的短短几周里，Papyrus 被叫作“Taterus”：由日语 tate（竖向）与“Papyrus”组合而成。但这个名字听起来太牵强，也不太好笑，所以没用多久就放弃了。

source.text: Even after deciding to keep Papyrus' name as-is, the team faced a new issue: "papyrus" is a foreign word to begin with, so how should Papyrus' Japanese name be pronounced? Should it follow the English pronunciation or the Japanese pronunciation (roughly "pah pee roos")? The team chose the latter.

name be pronounced? Should it follow the English pronunciation or the
Japanese pronunciation (roughly "pah pee roos")? The team chose the latter.

translation.text: 即使决定保留 Papyrus 的名字，团队仍遇到了一个新问题：“papyrus”（纸莎草）本来就是外来词，那么日语中这个名字该怎么念？是遵循英语发音，还是采用日语发音（大致是“pah pee roos”）？团队选择了后者。

source.text: Sans and Papyrus are brothers, but which is the older brother and which is the younger brother? The English script leaves this unclear - they're simply brothers. What's more, Toby had intended for the brothers' relationship to remain unclear.
source.raw:
Sans and Papyrus are brothers, but which is the older brother and which is
the younger brother? The English script leaves this unclear - they're simply
brothers. What's more, Toby had intended for the brothers' relationship to
remain unclear.

translation.text: Sans 和 Papyrus 是兄弟，但谁是哥哥、谁是弟弟？英文剧本没有说清，只知道他们是兄弟。而且 Toby 本来就打算让他们的长幼关系保持模糊。

source.text: Unfortunately, the brothers' uncertain relationship presented a major translation problem: there are words for "younger brother" and "older brother" in Japanese, but not for "brother" in general. Rather than make a blind guess, the translator consulted with Toby for details. Thus, through the translation process, it was definitively revealed that Sans is the older brother and Papyrus is the younger brother.
source.raw:
Unfortunately, the brothers' uncertain relationship presented a major
translation problem: there are words for "younger brother" and "older brother"
in Japanese, but not for "brother" in general. Rather than make a blind guess,
the translator consulted with Toby for details. Thus, through the translation
process, it was definitively revealed that Sans is the older brother and Papyrus
is the younger brother.

translation.text: 可惜，这种模糊关系造成了一个很大的翻译难题：日语有“弟弟”和“哥哥”的说法，却没有泛指单个“brother”的词。译者没有盲猜，而是向 Toby 询问详情。于是，通过翻译过程，Sans 是哥哥、Papyrus 是弟弟这件事才被明确揭晓。

translation.text: 这里英语只说“sister”（姐妹），日语则用“ねえさん”（nēsan，姐姐）。

source.text: This same relationship issue appeared elsewhere during Underta/e's Japanese localization. For example, a store owner mentions that she has a sister who manages the inn. In English, these two are simply referred to as sisters, but the Japanese language only has words for "younger sister" or "older sister".

This same relationship issue appeared elsewhere during Underta/e's Japanese
localization. For example, a store owner mentions that she has a sister who
manages the inn. In English, these two are simply referred to as sisters, but the

translation.text: Undertale 的日语本地化中，其他地方也遇到了相同的亲属关系问题。例如，一位店主提到，她的姐妹经营着旅馆。英语只说明两人是姐妹，但日语需要区分“妹妹”或“姐姐”。

source.text: Again, the translator consulted with Toby to determine their relationship. Toby had never considered how these sisters relate age-wise, so he arbitrarily decided that the store owner is the younger sister and the innkeeper is the older sister.

Again, the translator consulted with Toby to determine their relationship. Toby
had never considered how these sisters relate age-wise, so he arbitrarily decided

translation.text: 译者再次询问 Toby，以确定她们的关系。Toby 从未想过这对姐妹谁大谁小，于是随意决定店主是妹妹，旅馆老板是姐姐。

source.text: In short, there are parts of the Japanese script that provide small details not present in the English script - not because anything was intentionally changed, but simply because of how the two languages work.
source.raw:
In short, there are parts of the Japanese script that provide small details not

source.text: Based on Toby’s suggestion, the translator renamed the monster owaraichō, a combination of owarai ("comedy") and chō ("bird"). This name is also a play on the word raichō ("rock ptarmigan"), a bird associated with cold, snowy areas.

translation.text: Icecap 的日文名利用了“帽”（bō，帽子）与“坊”（bō，小子）的同音。

source.text: A monster named "Icecap" sometimes appears in battle. He wears a hat made of ice that he considers his pride and joy. In Japanese, Icecap’s name became hyōbō - hyō means "ice", while bō is a play on the Japanese words for "cap" and "boy". This is an interesting, rare example of a name that works perfectly in a straightforward translation. Not only that, the Japanese name naturally contains an extra layer of wordplay not found in the English version.
source.raw:
A monster named "Icecap" sometimes appears in battle. He wears a hat made
of ice that he considers his pride and joy. In Japanese, Icecap's name became
hy6b6 - hyo means "ice", while bo is a play on the Japanese words for "cap"
and "boy". This is an interesting, rare example of a name that works perfectly
in a straightforward translation. Not only that, the Japanese name naturally
contains an extra layer of wordplay not found in the English version.

translation.text: 战斗中有时会出现名叫“Icecap”的怪物。他戴着一顶冰做的帽子，对此引以为傲、爱不释手。日语中，Icecap 的名字变成了 hyōbō：hyō 是“冰”，bō 则同时指“帽子”和“小子”。这是个有趣而少见的例子，名字直译就能完美成立。不仅如此，日文名还自然地多出了一层英语版没有的双关。

source.text: Osaka is the name of a major city and a prefecture in western Japan. The Osaka metropolitan area is the second largest in Japan, after Tokyo.

This division includes language, too - the Japanese dialect associated with Osaka sounds significantly different from the more "standardized" Tokyo dialect.

translation.text: Sans 解释，战斗中的蓝色攻击不会伤害静止不动的玩家。然后，他提供了一个毫无必要地复杂的记忆方法：

source.text: imagine a stop sign. when you see a stop sign, you stop, right? stop signs are red. so imagine a blue stop sign. simple, right? when.fighting, think about blue stop signs.
source.raw:
imagine a stop sign. when you see a stop sign, you stop, right?
stop signs are red. so imagine a blue stop sign. simple, right?
when.fighting, think about blue stop signs.

translation.text: 想象一个停车标志。看到停车标志，你会停下，对吧？停车标志是红色的。那么，想象一个蓝色停车标志。简单吧？战斗时就想想蓝色停车标志。

source.text: Stop signs are red in Japan too, so this hint would be easy to translate into Japanese without any major issues. However, the translator felt the information would "click" more naturally in Japanese if it referred to a stoplight instead of a stop sign. Thus the line became:
source.raw:
Stop signs are red in Japan too, so this hint would be easy to translate
into Japanese without any major issues. However, the translator felt the
information would "click" more naturally in Japanese if it referred to a
stoplight instead of a stop sign. Thus the line became:

translation.text: 日本的停车标志也是红色，因此这条提示直接翻成日语也不会有什么大问题。不过，译者觉得，用交通信号灯代替停车标志，日本玩家会更容易“明白过来”。于是台词变成了：

source.text: everyone stops when a stoplight turns red, right? red stoplights mean "stop", but think ofb lue as "stop", okay? simple, right? in battle, blue means "stop".
source.raw:
everyone stops when a stoplight turns red, right?
red stoplights mean "stop", but think ofb lue as "stop", okay?
simple, right? in battle, blue means "stop".

translation.text: 日版大意是：信号灯变红，大家就会停下，对吧？红灯表示“停”，不过把蓝色当成“停”，好吗？简单吧？战斗时，蓝色就表示“停”。

source.text: This new text doesn't really seem to be that different from the original text, but there's a cultural reason behind it: in Japanese, green stoplights are called blue stoplights. And since real-life "blue" stoplights and red stoplights are opposites, it makes sense for Sans to swap the two in his overly complicated explanation.
source.raw:
This new text doesn't really seem to be that different from the original text,
but there's a cultural reason behind it: in Japanese, green stoplights are called
blue stoplights. And since real-life "blue" stoplights and red stoplights are
opposites, it makes sense for Sans to swap the two in his overly complicated
explanation.

translation.text: 新台词乍看与原文没什么不同，但背后有一个文化原因：日语会把绿色交通灯叫作蓝灯。现实中的“蓝灯”与红灯意思相反，因此 Sans 在那番过分复杂的解释里把两者对调，就说得通了。

source.text: For linguistic and historical reasons, the Japanese word 青 (ao) usually means "blue" in English, but can instead mean "green" in some situations. In general, ao means "green" when referring to plants, fruits, vegetables, and other types of "vibrant" green. Ao can also mean "green" in relation to other things, including stoplights and being new to something.
source.raw:

to other things, including stoplights and being new to something.

source.text: In English, the word "eliminate" usually means "to get rid of something" or even "to kill", but in some contexts - such as when discussing physiology or animal training- it can mean "to expel waste matter from the body". source.text: In the English version of Undertale, Snowdin's inn is aptly named the "Snowed Inn". Toby knew this pun would likely be lost in translation, so he suggested an alternative name: "Snowtel". The translator agreed that this combination of the English words "snow" and "hotel" would be more recognizable to Japanese players. However, this change also meant that that English-speaking players and Japanese-speaking players would know the same place by a different name.

an alternative name: "Snowtel". The translator agreed that this combination of
the English words "snow" and "hotel" would be more recognizable to Japanese
players. However, this change also meant that that English-speaking players
and Japanese-speaking players would know the same place by a different name.

translation.text: 英语版 Undertale 中，Snowdin 的旅馆恰如其分地叫作“Snowed Inn”。Toby 知道这个双关很可能在翻译中丢失，于是建议替代名称“Snowtel”。译者也认为，把英语 snow（雪）与 hotel（旅馆）组合起来，更容易让日本玩家理解。不过，这一改动也意味着，英语玩家和日语玩家会用不同名字称呼同一个地方。

source.text: Snowdin’s library is denoted by a large sign that says "LIBRARBY". This is a simple, childish misspelling of the English word "library" that some hasty players might not notice immediately. To achieve the same effect in Japanese, the localizers replaced the misspelled English sign with a similarly misspelled Japanese sign. Instead of としょかん (toshokan, "library"), the new sign says としょんか (toshonka), a hilariously bad misspelling that means nothing.

Small animals are counted with ~ (hiki)

Flat things are counted with t:z (mai)

• 大动物：頭（tō）
• 蝴蝶：不知为何也用頭（tō）

• 扁平物体：枚（mai）

source.text: In the English Undertale script, the bear says "those two married dogs" and "those two" when referring to Dogamy and Dogaressa, but how should they be counted in Japanese? The dogs walk and talk like people, which would warrant the counter word nin. But you can also pet them and play fetch with them like ordinary dogs, which would warrant hiki. So which should it be? And, perhaps more importantly, how would the Underground's denizens count them?
source.raw:
In the English Undertale script, the bear says "those two married dogs" and
"those two" when referring to Dogamy and Dogaressa, but how should they be
counted in Japanese? The dogs walk and talk like people, which would warrant
the counter word nin. But you can also pet them and play fetch with them like
ordinary dogs, which would warrant hiki. So which should it be? And, perhaps
more importantly, how would the Underground's denizens count them?

translation.text: 英文中，这只熊用“那对狗夫妻”和“那两个”指代 Dogamy 与 Dogaressa。日语该用哪个量词呢？它们像人一样走路、说话，似乎该用“人”；但它们又会让人抚摸、玩捡东西的游戏，似乎该用“匹”。更重要的是，地下世界的居民会怎样看待它们？

source.text: In the earliest drafts of the Japanese script, the translator chose hiki when referring to Dogamy and Dogaressa. Another team member later argued for using nin instead, given that they act overall more like people than dogs. The translator agreed and changed every instance of hiki to nin ... but accidentally missed one. As a result, the bear refers to the dogs as people and as small animals in the final draft of the Japanese script.
source.raw:
In the earliest drafts of the Japanese script, the translator chose hiki when
referring to Dogamy and Dogaressa. Another team member later argued for
using nin instead, given that they act overall more like people than dogs. The
translator agreed and changed every instance of hiki to nin ... but accidentally
missed one. As a result, the bear refers to the dogs as people and as small
animals in the final draft of the Japanese script.

translation.text: 最早的译稿用了“匹”。后来，有位团队成员认为它们更像人，应该用“人”。团队于是作了替换，却漏改了一处。最终版里，这只熊既把它们当作人来数，也把它们当作小动物来数。

blocks.notes: 标题结合本页 hitbox 语境的暂译。

source.text: During this battle, the player must dodge bones that scroll by quickly and spell a funny phrase

translation.text: 在这场战斗中，玩家必须躲开快速掠过的骨头；这些骨头还拼成了一句有趣的话。

source.text: In battle, Papyrus repeatedly and humorously states that he has a special attack that he’s prepared to use if need be. Eventually, he unleashes his special attack, which is flashy, strange, and funny all at once. In the English version of Undertale, this attack ends with the eight-character message “COOL DUDE” spelled out in bones. The player must then dodge this text as it quickly scrolls by.

translation.text: 战斗中，Papyrus 一再以诙谐的方式宣称，自己备有一招特殊攻击，必要时就会使出来。最后，他终于使出了这招既华丽、又古怪、还很好笑的攻击。在英文版 Undertale 中，攻击最后会出现用骨头拼出的八个字符：“COOL DUDE”（酷哥）。这行字会快速掠过，玩家必须躲开。

source.text: Because this English bone text is somewhat difficult to read and scrolls by quickly, the translator felt it would benefit the gameplay experience to localize the bone text into Japanese. But as Toby noted, any changes to “COOL DUDE” would likely change the difficulty of avoiding the scrolling text. With this in mind, the translator looked for a phrase that could say roughly the same thing in Japanese using the exact same number of characters as the English message.

translation.text: 这些英文骨头字有些难读，移动又快，因此译者认为，将它们本地化成日文会改善游玩体验。但正如 Toby 所指出的，任何对“COOL DUDE”的改动，都可能改变躲避这行移动文字的难度。考虑到这一点，译者开始寻找一个日文短语：意思大致相同，字符数也必须与英文完全一致。

source.text: Papyrus has a “COOL DUDE” attack and wears a “COOL DUDE” outfit at one point, but localizing the attack text into Japanese broke this connection

translation.text: Papyrus 有一招“COOL DUDE”攻击，还曾穿过写着“COOL DUDE”的衣服。不过，把攻击文字本地化成日文后，两者之间的呼应就消失了。

source.text: After some brainstorming for a replacement message, the translator chose the phrase イカした こうげき (ikashita kōgeki), which roughly means “cool attack” or “totally sweet attack”. This phrase was then given to the game art studio 256graph to transform into graphical form. 256graph not only created all-new Japanese bone text, but also ensured that its height and width closely matched the height and width of the original English bone text.

translation.text: 经过一番构思，译者选定了“イカした こうげき”（ikashita kōgeki），大意是“很酷的攻击”或“超棒的攻击”。随后，这个短语交给游戏美术工作室 256graph 制作成图像。256graph 不仅制作了全新的日文骨头字，还确保其高度和宽度与原英文骨头字尽量接近。

blocks.notes: 日文与罗马字保留；本页截图和骨头字图像均保留原样。

source.text: They definitely don’t teach hit box localization in textbooks or school, this is uncharted territory for almost everyone

translation.text: 教科书或学校里肯定不会教你如何本地化碰撞判定框；对几乎所有人来说，这都是陌生的领域。

source.text: The localized Japanese bone text closely matches the dimensions of the original English bone text

translation.text: 本地化后的日文骨头字，尺寸与原英文骨头字十分接近。

source.text: All of this teamwork resulted in a Japanese phrase with the same number of characters as the English phrase, hitboxes that closely match the original game’s hitboxes, and all-new bone graphics that look just like the original English bone graphics. Even more impressive is that all of this work was done for one short message that stays on the screen for less than five seconds!

translation.text: 经过这番协作，最终的日文短语与英文拥有相同的字符数，碰撞判定框也与原版十分接近；全新制作的骨头字图像，看起来仍与原英文版本风格一致。更令人佩服的是，这一切工作，只是为了屏幕上一句停留不到五秒钟的短语！

typography.method: Original PDF rendered at 2100px, measured text ink rows, fixed paragraph starts and unchanged illustrations; visual comparison required.
typography.visual_reference: Two user-provided generated pages: chapter introduction and localization note; matching type rhythm, not copying their wording.
typography.line_break: Paragraph dynamic programming; measured fonts; punctuation trimming; CJK/word expansion only

source.text: WELCOME TO SCENIC MY HOUSE!
source.raw: WELCOME TO SCENIC MY HOUSE!

source.text: This is a humorous reference to the stereotypical signs found at American tourist destinations, such as "Welcome to historic Licking, Missouri" and "Welcome to scenic Boogertown, North Carolina". Naturally, referring to the inside of one's home as a scenic tourist destination sounds ridiculous. The entire English sentence sounds off-kilter at first, too.
source.raw:
This is a humorous reference to the stereotypical signs found at American
tourist destinations, such as "Welcome to historic Licking, Missouri" and
"Welcome to scenic Boogertown, North Carolina". Naturally, referring to the
inside of one's home as a scenic tourist destination sounds ridiculous. The
entire English sentence sounds off-kilter at first, too.

translation.text: 这句玩笑模仿了美国旅游景点常见的欢迎标语，例如“欢迎来到历史悠久的密苏里州利金市”和“欢迎来到风景秀丽的北卡罗来纳州 Boogertown”。把自己家里说成景色优美的旅游胜地，自然很荒唐。而且整句英语一开始听起来也有点别扭。

source.text: Japanese tourist spots don't follow the same phrasing pattern to welcome visitors, so the original cultural reference was lost in translation. The core joke of calling one's home "scenic" works in any language, though, so this line was given a simple, straightforward translation into Japanese.
source.raw:
Japanese tourist spots don't follow the same phrasing pattern to welcome
visitors, so the original cultural reference was lost in translation. The core joke
of calling one's home "scenic" works in any language, though, so this line was
given a simple, straightforward translation into Japanese.

translation.text: 日本景点欢迎游客时不用相同的句式，所以这个文化典故在翻译中丢失了。但把自家称为“风景秀丽”的核心笑点，在任何语言里都成立，因此日文直接译出了这句话。

source.text: As we've seen, English words appear all the time in Japanese games. Over the years, these English words have formed a limited "English game vocabulary" that Japanese gamers naturally absorb. However, it's still common for English phrases to be simplified during English-to Japanese game localization.

Japanese game localization.

translation.text: 前面已经看到，日本游戏中经常出现英语词。多年来，它们形成了一套范围有限的“游戏英语词汇”，日本玩家玩着玩着就熟悉了。不过，英语游戏本地化成日语时，简化英文措辞仍然十分常见。

source.text: Conversely, "flawless" was kept intact in the Japanese version of One Step From Eden (2020), but the phrase "battle won" was simplified to "victory"

source.text: As we've already seen, the translation process can reveal details not found in the original work. In this case, because the Japanese language is based on syllables and not sounds, a standard translation of "can I speak to G?" into Japanese would result in a vowel appearing after "G". This would reveal more information about G's identity - enough for fans to solve this mystery. Toby understood this, and eventually firmly requested that this text remain completely in English. And, as he suggested, leaving it in English would make the line feel even stranger for Japanese players.

in the original work. In this case, because the Japanese language is based on
syllables and not sounds, a standard translation of "can I speak to G?" into

more information about G's identity - enough for fans to solve this mystery.
Toby understood this, and eventually firmly requested that this text remain

source.text: This prank call based on an English pun wouldn't work in Japanese, so the translator replaced it with a reference to Licca-chan, a classic Japanese toy doll famous for having a real-life telephone hotline. In Japanese, Onionsan ends sentences in a way that's associated with
childishness, silliness, and awkward nerdiness. The Japanese script also treats
the "san" part of"Onionsan" as the Japanese name suffix -san, which is roughly
equivalent to "Mr." or "Ms." In English. However, it's improper to add -san
when saying your own name, so this localization choice adds another layer of
social awkwardness to the character.

translation.text: 日语中，Onionsan 的句尾带着孩子气、傻乎乎又不擅交际的宅气。译文还把“Onionsan”里的 san 视作日语姓名后缀 -san，大致相当于英语的 Mr. 或 Ms.（先生／女士）。然而，说自己的名字时不应加 -san，所以这一处理又给角色添了一层不通人情世故的感觉。

source.text: As with several other characters in Undertale, Onionsan's gender is meant to be unclear. As such, Onionsan usually uses the polite, somewhat gender neutral Japanese pronoun watashi. On other occasions, Onionsan simply says "Onionsan" instead of using a pronoun, which lends the character even more of a childish vibe.

source.text: For various technical and historical reasons, early Japanese computing systems used "half-width characters". These squished characters allowed two characters to fit in the space of one standard character. This came at a cost, however: the half-width character set only supports one Japanese writing system: katakana.

source.text: This is a humorous reference to a famous food in Japan called daigaku imo, which translates as "college potato" or "university potato". Daigaku imo is basically deep-fried sweet potato covered with a hard sugar coating. It first gained popularity in the 1900s as an inexpensive, but filling meal for Japanese university students, and has since become a standard dish that can be found in countless recipe books, restaurants, and food stalls throughout Japan.

source.text: An intimidating knight named Undyne first appears in Waterfall. She loathes the main character at first, but the player can change her attitude over time. As such, Undyne sounds scary and ferocious in some situations, polite and friendly in others, and sometimes all of these things at once. Luckily, Toby provided many notes about Undyne's constant attitude changes.
source.raw:
An intimidating knight named Undyne first appears in Waterfall. She loathes
the main character at first, but the player can change her attitude over time.
As such, Undyne sounds scary and ferocious in some situations, polite and
friendly in others, and sometimes all of these things at once. Luckily, Toby
provided many notes about Undyne's constant attitude changes.

translation.text: 令人畏惧的骑士 Undyne 首次登场于瀑布。起初她厌恶主角，但玩家可以逐渐改变她的态度。因此，Undyne 有时凶狠可怕，有时礼貌友好，有时甚至兼而有之。幸好，Toby 对她不断变化的态度留下了许多说明。

source.text: In Japanese, Undyne uses the pronoun watashi. This suits her in several ways:
source.raw: In Japanese, Undyne uses the pronoun watashi. This suits her in several ways:

translation.text: 日语中，Undyne 使用 watashi（我）自称，在几个方面都很合适：

source.text: It conveys a sense of neutral courtesy, professionalism, and honor In some contexts it can give off a sense of femininity It can be safely used in a wide variety of situations
source.raw:
It conveys a sense of neutral courtesy, professionalism, and honor
In some contexts it can give off a sense of femininity
It can be safely used in a wide variety of situations

translation.text:
• 传达中性、礼貌、专业、重荣誉的感觉。
• 某些语境下，也能显出女性气质。
• 适用范围广，在各种场合都不容易出错。

source.text: Of course, other pronouns could've suited Undyne too - one interesting solution might've been to give her a different pronoun to match her different attitudes.
source.raw:
Of course, other pronouns could've suited Undyne too - one interesting solution
might've been to give her a different pronoun to match her different attitudes.

translation.text: 当然，其他人称代词也可能适合 Undyne。有个有趣的办法，或许是让她随态度变化，使用不同的自称。

translation.text: 与 Papyrus 的笑声一样，Undyne 发怒时的吼声在日文剧本里也稍作了调整。

source.text: In the English script, Undyne often shouts "ngaaaah" when frustrated. Because grunts, growls, and other sounds often "feel" different in different languages, Undyne's growls were translated as nuaaaa throughout the Japanese script.
source.raw:
In the English script, Undyne often shouts "ngaaaah" when frustrated. Because
grunts, growls, and other sounds often "feel" different in different languages,
Undyne's growls were translated as nuaaaa throughout the Japanese script.

translation.text: 英语剧本中，Undyne 恼火时经常大吼“ngaaaah”。哼声、吼声等声音在不同语言中，往往给人不同的“感觉”，因此日文剧本把她的吼声统一译成 nuaaaa。

source.text: I feel like an analysis of the zillion different sounds of Japanese laughter could fill its own little textbook
source.raw:
I feel like an analysis
of the zillion different
sounds of Japanese
laughter could fill its
own little textbook

translation.text: 我觉得，光分析日语里千奇百怪的笑声，就够写一本小教材了。

source.text: Undyne also tends to laugh when she's confident. In English, this laugh is spelled "fuhuhu". In Japanese,fuhuhu is sometimes associated with polite, friendly laughter and cordial giggling, so the translator localizedfuhuhu as kukukuku, which carries a sense of confidence, stubbornness, and/or cunning.
source.raw:
Undyne also tends to laugh when she's confident. In English, this laugh is
spelled "fuhuhu". In Japanese,fuhuhu is sometimes associated with polite,
friendly laughter and cordial giggling, so the translator localizedfuhuhu as
kukukuku, which carries a sense of confidence, stubbornness, and/or cunning.

translation.text: Undyne 信心十足时也常会大笑。英语把这笑声写作“fuhuhu”。但在日语中，fuhuhu 有时让人想到礼貌、友好的笑声或亲切的轻笑。于是译者改用了 kukukuku，这种笑声带有自信、倔强或狡黠的意味。

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: Chrono Trigger
source.raw: Inspiration Spotlight: Chrono Trigger

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：Chrono Trigger

source.text: In 1995, Square released Chrono Trigger for the Japanese Super Famicom and the North American Super NES. This classic, influential Japanese RPG introduced new gameplay concepts not found in its contemporaries, including time-travel mechanics, branching storylines, and multi character battle techniques. As the product of a dream team of game developers, Chrono Trigger enjoyed commercial and critical success upon release, and remains well regarded to this day.
source.raw:
In 1995, Square released Chrono Trigger for the Japanese Super Famicom
and the North American Super NES. This classic, influential Japanese
RPG introduced new gameplay concepts not found in its contemporaries,
including time-travel mechanics, branching storylines, and multi
character battle techniques. As the product of a dream team of game
developers, Chrono Trigger enjoyed commercial and critical success upon
release, and remains well regarded to this day.

translation.text: 1995 年，Square 在日本 Super Famicom 与北美 Super NES 平台发行了 Chrono Trigger。这部经典日式 RPG 影响深远，加入了当时同类作品未见的玩法构想，包括时间旅行机制、分支剧情，以及多人合体战技。它由游戏开发者组成的梦之队打造，上市时销量与口碑俱佳，至今仍备受推崇。

translation.text: 读者挑战 6：给冰淇淋车的曲子填一段自己的“消灭敌人”歌词。

source.text: Undyne offers the main character a drink. Options include tea, hot chocolate, soda, and a cup of sugar. If the player selects the cup of sugar, Undyne says in English:
source.raw:
Undyne offers the main character a drink. Options include tea, hot chocolate, soda,
and a cup of sugar. If the player selects the cup of sugar, Undyne says in English:

translation.text: Undyne 请主角喝点东西，可选茶、热巧克力、汽水和一杯糖。如果选那杯糖，英语版中 Undyne 会说：

source.text: I'm not gonna give you a cup ofs ugar! What do I look like, the ice-cream woman? Do human ice-cream women TERRORIZE HUMANITY with ENERGY SPEARS? Are their ice-cream songs a PRELUDE TO DESTRUCTION?
source.raw:
I'm not gonna give you a cup ofs ugar! What do I look like, the ice-cream
woman? Do human ice-cream women TERRORIZE HUMANITY
with ENERGY SPEARS? Are their ice-cream songs a PRELUDE TO
DESTRUCTION?

translation.text: 我才不会给你一杯糖！你当我是卖冰淇淋的女人吗？人类世界卖冰淇淋的女人，会用能量长矛让全人类闻风丧胆吗？她们的冰淇淋歌，是毁灭的序曲吗？

source.text: The joke here is part of a larger running gag: Undyne imagines the human world to be just like what's depicted in fiction-based anime and manga. And in this scene, she equates happy ice cream truck music with a human warrior's "death to the enemy" song.
source.raw:
The joke here is part of a larger running gag: Undyne imagines the human
world to be just like what's depicted in fiction-based anime and manga. And in
this scene, she equates happy ice cream truck music with a human warrior's
"death to the enemy" song.

translation.text: 这处笑料延续了游戏里反复出现的一个梗：Undyne 以为，人类世界就像虚构的动画和漫画描绘的那样。因此在这里，她把冰淇淋车欢快的音乐，当成了人类战士的“消灭敌人”之歌。

source.text: Although ice cream trucks represent a commonly shared cultural experience in many Western countries, they're culturally insignificant in Japan. This left the localization team in a tough situation: Undyne's line needs to be related to sugar, a literal translation wouldn't make much sense, and there's no strong equivalent to musical ice cream trucks in Japanese culture. For this reason, early drafts of the Japanese scripts had Undyne talk about how warriors in the human world surely sell ice cream and work in ice cream shops.
source.raw:
Although ice cream trucks represent a commonly shared cultural experience
in many Western countries, they're culturally insignificant in Japan. This left
the localization team in a tough situation: Undyne's line needs to be related
to sugar, a literal translation wouldn't make much sense, and there's no strong
equivalent to musical ice cream trucks in Japanese culture. For this reason,
early drafts of the Japanese scripts had Undyne talk about how warriors in the
human world surely sell ice cream and work in ice cream shops.

translation.text: 冰淇淋车在许多西方国家是共同的文化记忆，在日本却没什么文化分量。这给本地化团队出了难题：Undyne 的台词必须与糖有关，直译说不通，日本文化里也找不到足以对应音乐冰淇淋车的事物。因此，日文剧本的早期译稿让 Undyne 说，人类世界的战士一定会卖冰淇淋、在冰淇淋店工作。

source.text: Later, a localization team member noted that Undyne's new line felt too plain in comparison to the original. The line was then updated to suggest that human warriors surely eat ice cream before charging into battle.
source.raw:
Later, a localization team member noted that Undyne's new line felt too plain
in comparison to the original. The line was then updated to suggest that
human warriors surely eat ice cream before charging into battle.

translation.text: 后来，一位团队成员觉得，新台词与原文相比太平淡，于是又改成了人类战士一定会在冲上战场前吃冰淇淋。

source.text: Soon after, another team member suggested replacing the ice cream truck with a food vehicle that is more common in Japan: a yakiimo ("roasted sweet potato") truck. This idea was dropped, however, because it lacked a clear, logical connection to normal sugar.
source.raw:
Soon after, another team member suggested replacing the ice cream truck
with a food vehicle that is more common in Japan: ayakiimo ("roasted sweet
potato") truck. This idea wa dropped, however, because it lacked a clear,
logical connection to normal sugar.

translation.text: 不久，另一位成员提议，把冰淇淋车换成日本更常见的 yakiimo（烤红薯）车。不过，烤红薯与普通砂糖之间没有清楚、合理的联系，这个方案也被放弃了。

source.text: After even more discussion, the translator changed Undyne's line to reference a classic Japanese snack instead of ice cream trucks:
source.raw:
After even more discussion, the translator changed Undyne's line to reference a
classic Japanese snack instead of ice cream trucks:

translation.text: 经过更多讨论，译者最终用日本经典零食，取代了冰淇淋车的典故：

source.text: Who the hell pours sugar into a cup and offers it to a guest?! What, do you plan on sipping it with a spoon or something? I mean, I've heard ofp eople with a sweet-tooth before, but this is on a different level. Or do sweets on the surface world make you strong, let you sprint for 300 meters, and other stuff like that?
source.raw:

plan on sipping it with a spoon or something? I mean, I've heard ofp eople

source.text: This new text refers to Japanese Glico-brand snacks and their two timeless slogans: "makes you strong" and "300 meters in a single piece".

polite speech patterns that fit her character. Alphys also uses the polite and

translation.text: 英文剧本中的科学家 Alphys 谈到工作时聪明而专业，闲聊时却害羞、宅气又不自信。译者把符合她性格的随意说法和礼貌说法混合起来，在日语中表现这些特点。Alphys 自称时还使用礼貌、略带女性色彩的代词 watashi（我）。

source.text: Early on, Toby noted that "Alphys" should be pronounced "al-feez", which he imagined would be spelled in Japanese as アルフィーズ (arufīzu). He also understood that this six-character name could cause problems with Papyrus’ vertical text box, which only comfortably allows five characters per line. Thus, per Toby’s personal suggestion, Alphys is now known as アルフィー (arufī, roughly: "Alphy") in the Japanese script. Naturally, this name change surprised early Japanese fans who were accustomed to seeing Alphys’ full name in the fan-made translations.

vertical text box, which only comfortably allows five characters per line. Thus,

source.text: Underta/e's English script sometimes uses the Japanese word tsundere. In broad terms, tsundere - roughly pronounced "tsoon deh reh" - describes the trait of having an unfriendly attitude on the outside that gives way to an affectionate inner attitude over time.

translation.text: 《Undertale》的英文剧本偶尔会用日语词 tsundere（傲娇，读音大致是“tsoon deh reh”）。广义上，它形容一种性格：表面不友善，内心的亲昵却随着时间渐渐显露。

source.text: Twndere is a common word in Japanese entertainment, but is notoriously troublesome to translate into English because it has no solid equivalent. For this reason, English-speaking fans of Japanese entertainment - such as Toby - tend to leave the word untranslated. Basically, tsundere is in the process of becoming a loan word in English like "karate" and "karaoke", but it hasn't yet reached mainstream recognition. As such, the word tsundere might confuse some English-speaking players, but it poses little problem for Japanese players.
source.raw:

troublesome to translate into English because it has no solid equivalent. For
this reason, English-speaking fans of Japanese entertainment - such as Toby
- tend to leave the word untranslated. Basically, tsundere is in the process of
becoming a loan word in English like "karate" and "karaoke", but it hasn't yet
reached mainstream recognition. As such, the word tsundere might confuse
some English-speaking players, but it poses little problem for Japanese players.

source.text: In a 1997 English dub of a Dragon Ball Z episode, a villain angrily shouts, "It's over 9000!" after checking his opponent's power level. Over time, the quote also began to appear in mainstream English-language entertainment. It also began to appear in video games, including:

source.text: Overview of Japanese gyokai yogo
source.raw: Overview of Japanese gyokai yogo

translation.text: 日语行业行话一览

source.text: In simple terms, Japanese gyokai yoga, sometimes referred to as zujago, is similar to English "Pig Latin" -you basically shuffle and move the characters in a word to create a new, funny-sounding "secret code word".
source.raw:
In simple terms, Japanese gyokai yoga, sometimes referred to as zujago,
is similar to English "Pig Latin" -you basically shuffle and move the
characters in a word to create a new, funny-sounding "secret code word".

translation.text: 简单说，这种行话有时也叫 zūjago，类似英语的 Pig Latin（儿童黑话）：调换词内字符，造出一个听起来好笑的新“暗号词”。

source.text: In basic gyōkai yōgo, the final character in a word is moved to the front, and certain vowels are elongated. For example, トマト (tomato) might become トートマ (tōtoma), while スシ (sushi) might become シースー (shīsū).
source.raw:
In basic gyokai yogo, the final character in a word is moved to the front,
and certain vowels are elongated. For example, 1--~ 1-- (tomato) might
become f..-1--~ (totoma), while ;z~ (sushi) might become ~-;z- (shTsO).

translation.text: 最基本的做法是把词尾字符挪到前面，再拉长某些元音。例如「トマト」（tomato，番茄）可能变成「トートマ」（tōtoma）；「スシ」（sushi，寿司）则可能变成「シースー」（shīsū）。

source.text: Under normal circumstances, a professional translator would've immediately looked for the equivalent lines from the Japanese version of Kitchen. However, Toby specifically noted that he considered this text an "in-joke between friends" and that "since it's just a joke, you don't have to find the original". Under normal circumstances, a professional translator would've immediately
looked for the equivalent lines from the Japanese version of Kitchen. However,
Toby specifically noted that he considered this text an "in-joke between friends"
and that "since it's just a joke, you don't have to find the original". He further
emphasized this attitude elsewhere in the spreadsheet by saying "Another

source.text: Undertale's translator honored Toby's unusual wish and translated the guards' indirect English quotes back into Japanese as-is. This resulted in Japanese text that is recognizable as a Kitchen reference, but with noticeably different wording.
source.raw:
Undertale's translator honored Toby's unusual wish and translated the guards'
indirect English quotes back into Japanese as-is. This resulted in Japanese
text that is recognizable as a Kitchen reference, but with noticeably different
wording.

translation.text: 《Undertale》的译者尊重了 Toby 这个不寻常的愿望，把卫兵那几句不精确的英文照样译回日语。结果仍能看出是在引用《厨房》，但措辞明显不同。

source.text: Normally, skilled translators will go out of their way to retain jokes and references, as it's assumed that the original author considered them important enough to use. As such, it's rare to encounter a situation like this, in which the author is actually so unattached to a reference that the translators are asked to skip it! Toby truly is the king of crazy exceptions.
source.raw:

source.text: In English, Muffet uses tildes (the squiggly - mark) at the end of words to denote a cute, upbeat tone of voice. This use of tildes is still uncommon in English, which lends Muffet a distinctive vibe. Tilde-like characters are extremely common in Japanese entertainment, so Muffet retains her squiggles in the Japanese script. Basically, this tilde use is a good example of how Toby blended certain Japanese language quirks into Undertale's original English script.

translation.text: 日本漫才

source.text: Manzai is a long-established form of Japanese stand-up comedy that traditionally features a team of two comedians. Much like the double-act comedy routines found in other countries, manzai usually involves one bokeh ("funny man") and one tsukkomi ("straight man") playing off of each other as ridiculous situations unfold.
source.raw:
Manzai is a long-established form of Japanese stand-up comedy that
traditionally features a team of two comedians. Much like the double-act
comedy routines found in other countries, manzai usually involves one
bokeh ("funny man") and one tsukkomi ("straight man") playing off of
each other as ridiculous situations unfold.

translation.text: Manzai（漫才）是日本历史悠久的舞台喜剧形式，传统上由两名演员搭档。与其他国家的双人喜剧相似，漫才通常由 bokeh（装傻逗趣者）与 tsukkomi（吐槽纠正者）相互配合，演出荒唐情境。

source.text: Historically, manzai is approximately 1000 years old, but modern-day manzai emerged from Osaka in the early 1900s. From there, Osaka-style manzai spread to the rest of Japan via stage, radio, and other forms of entertainment.
source.raw:
Historically, manzai is approximately 1000 years old, but modern-day
manzai emerged from Osaka in the early 1900s. From there, Osaka-style
manzai spread to the rest of Japan via stage, radio, and other forms of
entertainment.

translation.text: 漫才的历史约有一千年，不过现代漫才是在 20 世纪初的大阪成形的。此后，大阪式漫才通过舞台、广播等娱乐形式传遍日本。

source.text: Today, manzai corporations play a major part in the Japanese entertainment industry by cultivating and introducing new talent. As such, many Japanese actors, singers, television hosts, and other celebrities begin their careers by making a name for themselves on the national manzai circuit.

source.text: Children in English-speaking regions are taught that "please" and "thank you" are "magic words" that should be used when making a request or after receiving something. source.text: Because "please" and "thank you" aren't traditionally called "magic words" in Japanese, the translator changed Madjick's "please and thank you" to popopopo-n. This mostly meaningless word is a reference to Aisatsu no Maha ("Greetings Are Magic"), a magic-themed public service announcement that constantly aired on Japanese television in 2011.

source.text: Aisatsu no Maha on Japanese Television
source.raw: Aisatsu no Maha on Japanese Television

translation.text: 日本电视上的《问候的魔法》

source.text: In 2011, several regions of Japan were hit by devastating natural and manmade disasters. During this painful and turbulent time, many Japanese companies felt it would be inappropriate and tone-deaf to advertise their products on television between the constant news programs about the disasters. For this reason, ordinary commercials on television were often replaced with simple filler material.
source.raw:
In 2011, several regions of Japan were hit by devastating natural and
manmade disasters. During this painful and turbulent time, many Japanese
companies felt it would be inappropriate and tone-deaf to advertise their
products on television between the constant news programs about the
disasters. For this reason, ordinary commercials on television were often
replaced with simple filler material.

translation.text: 2011 年，日本多地遭受严重天灾与人祸。在这段痛苦、动荡的时期，许多企业觉得，在不断播报灾情的新闻之间插入商品广告很不合适，也显得不懂人情。因此，电视上的普通广告常被简单的填充节目取代。

source.text: One such "filler video" was Aisatsu no Maha ("Greetings Are Magic"), a 2010 children's song and television public service announcement that aired with brain-searing regularity in 2011. Aisatsu no Maha repeated on Japanese television so often that it became a widely shared cultural experience. The video grew so grating over time that it spawned hate memes, spooky urban legends, and elaborate conspiracy theories.

translation.text: 虚构拟声词 popopopo~n 因反复出现，与魔法紧密联系起来。

source.text: As a song, Aisatsu no Maha was intended to teach children the importance of words like konnichi wa ("hello"), itadakimasu ("I humbly accept this food"), and arigata ("thank you"). In the song, these phrases are referred to as "magic words" that can help you make friends. The lyrics also include the occasional popopopo-n, a made-up sound effect word that was intended to represent "the sound of lots of friends appearing". Popopopo-n was such an unavoidable phrase that it won first place in 2011 's Japanese Internet Buzzword Awards.

source.text: Word Problems

translation.text: 文字难题

source.text: What DO you like most about Mettaton? Write your answer below for future generations to read:

translation.text: 你究竟最喜欢 Mettaton 的哪一点？请把答案写在下面，留给后人阅读：

source.text: During battle, Mettaton gains a humanoid body and becomes Mettaton EX. He then stops and asks the player a question:

translation.text: 战斗中，Mettaton 获得了人形身体，变成 Mettaton EX。随后，他停下来问玩家一个问题：

source.text: “What do you love most about Mettaton?”

translation.text: “你最喜欢 Mettaton 的哪一点？”

source.text: The player is then asked to type an essay on their computer keyboard that answers this question. Once the essay is finished – or if time runs out – Mettaton EX will scan the player’s essay for specific keywords and respond with appropriate dialogue. Toby originally designed this system to recognize English answers, so getting it to work properly in Japanese required all-new programming code and technical adjustments.

translation.text: 接下来，玩家需要用电脑键盘输入一篇短文来回答这个问题。写完之后，或者时间一到，Mettaton EX 就会扫描玩家的文章，寻找特定关键词，并给出对应的回应。Toby 最初把这套系统设计为识别英文答案，因此，要让它正常处理日文，就需要编写全新的代码并作出技术调整。

source.text: Keyboards

translation.text: 键盘

source.text: First, because Undertale was originally designed for home computers, players could simply use their computer keyboard to type an essay answer. Unfortunately, home consoles rarely come with keyboards. To get around this hardware issue, the localization team added new code to Undertale’s programming to display on-screen keyboards compatible with game controllers.

translation.text: 首先，Undertale 最初是为家用电脑设计的，玩家可以直接用电脑键盘输入答案。然而，家用游戏机很少配备键盘。为了解决这一硬件问题，本地化团队为 Undertale 添加了新代码，显示可以用游戏手柄操作的屏幕键盘。

source.text: Japanese Input

translation.text: 日文输入

source.text: The Japanese language includes three separate writing systems, which complicates the process of searching for keywords in the player’s essay. For example, the word bibō (“good looks”) can be written with a combination of all three systems, leading to multiple possible spellings:

translation.text: 日语包含三种书写系统，这使得在玩家文章中搜索关键词变得复杂。例如，bibō（“美貌”）可以用这三种书写系统组合写出，因而有多种可能的写法：

source.text:
びぼう (all hiragana)
ビボウ (all katakana)
美貌 (all kanji)
美ぼう (kanji + hiragana)
美ボウ (kanji + katakana)
び貌 (hiragana + kanji)
ビ貌 (katakana + kanji)

translation.text:
びぼう（全平假名）
ビボウ（全片假名）
美貌（全汉字）
美ぼう（汉字＋平假名）
美ボウ（汉字＋片假名）
び貌（平假名＋汉字）
ビ貌（片假名＋汉字）

blocks.notes: 保留日文拼写；原位预览采用两栏列表。

source.text: To simplify this technical problem, the localization team disabled kanji support. The team then added new programming that internally converts every katakana character to hiragana.

translation.text: 为简化这一技术问题，本地化团队禁用了汉字支持，随后加入新程序，在内部把每个片假名字符转换成平假名。

source.text: This technical solution simplified matters greatly, but it had an unexpected flaw: the game’s core programming already uses the “Z” and “X” keys for other in-game functions. To get around this, the localization team made sure that no Japanese keywords required the “Z” or “X” keys. The team then added an on-screen message stating that “Z” and “X” are unavailable. Fortunately, these keys aren’t 100% vital for Japanese input to begin with – there are often multiple ways to type a single word in Japanese.

translation.text: 这项技术方案大大简化了问题，但也带来了一个意料之外的缺陷：游戏的核心程序已经把“Z”和“X”键用于其他游戏功能。为此，本地化团队确保所有日文关键词都不必用到“Z”或“X”键，并增加了提示，说明这两个键不可用。幸好，日文输入并非一定需要它们——同一个日语词往往有多种输入方式。

source.text: The capital "T" in "The Locket" might seem like a simple typo at first, making it easy for players - and translators - to overlook its importance. What's more, the Japanese language lacks both uppercase writing and articles like "a" and "the". Had Underta/e's localization been rushed, this combination of language quirks could've easily led to a generic-sounding game phrase:

The capital "T" in "The Locket" might seem like a simple typo at first, making
it easy for players - and translators - to overlook its importance. What's more,
the Japanese language lacks both uppercase writing and articles like "a" and

translation.text: “The Locket”里大写的 T，乍看可能只是笔误，玩家和译者都很容易忽略它的重要性。日语既没有字母大小写，也没有 a、the 这样的冠词。假如《Undertale》的本地化赶工，这些语言差异凑在一起，很容易把它译成一句毫无特殊意味的游戏提示：

source.raw: Got [a/the] locket.

translation.text: 得到了挂坠。

source.text: The secret lab is equipped with an ominous device known as the "DT Extraction Machine" in English. The player is supposed to deduce that "DT" stands for "Determination".
source.raw:
The secret lab is equipped with an ominous device known as the "DT
Extraction Machine" in English. The player is supposed to deduce that "DT"
stands for "Determination".

translation.text: 秘密实验室里有一台不祥的装置，英文名为“DT Extraction Machine”（DT 提取机）。玩家需要自行推断，DT 代表 Determination（决心）。

source.text: Because "determination" was translated as ketsui elsewhere in the Japanese script, this machine was renamed the "KTI Extraction Machine". This peculiar abbreviation comes from how ketsui is spelled in the Japanese script: ケツイ (Ke Tsu I).
source.raw:
Because "determination" was translated as ketsui elsewhere in the Japanese
script, this machine was renamed the "KTI Extraction Machine". This peculiar
abbreviation comes from how ketsui is spelled in the Japanese script:
7""/1 (Ke Tsu I).

translation.text: 日文剧本的其他地方把 determination 译成了 ketsui（决心），因此这台机器也改名为“KTI 提取机”。这个特别的缩写来自游戏里 ketsui 的写法：「ケツイ」（Ke Tsu I），各取一个字母。

source.text: This simple localization change offers another example of how a single localization choice in one part of a script can unexpectedly affect other parts. Such unexpected side effects can easily be missed by machine translation systems, rushed translators using primitive "search-and-replace" tools, or inexperienced translators.
source.raw:
This simple localization change offers another example of how a single
localization choice in one part of a script can unexpectedly affect other parts.
Such unexpected side effects can easily be missed by machine translation
systems, rushed translators using primitive "search-and-replace" tools, or
inexperienced translators.

translation.text: 这个简单的改动再次说明，剧本某一处的翻译选择，可能意外影响其他地方。机器翻译、用简陋“查找替换”工具赶工的译者，或经验不足的译者，都很容易漏掉这类连带影响。

source.text: The Dangers of Search-and-Replace in Translation
source.raw: The Dangers of Search-and-Replace in Translation

source.text: In today's computer age, writers regularly rely on automatic spell-checking and search-and-replace tools to fix problematic text. Translators rely on these tools all the time, too. Of course, these tools can actually introduce new problems into a translation if used improperly. This phenomenon is rare, but when it occurs, it can harm the quality of the full, final product.
source.raw:
In today's computer age, writers regularly rely on automatic spell-checking
and search-and-replace tools to fix problematic text. Translators rely on
these tools all the time, too. Of course, these tools can actually introduce
new problems into a translation if used improperly. This phenomenon is
rare, but when it occurs, it can harm the quality of the full, final product.

translation.text: 在电脑时代，作者经常用自动拼写检查、查找替换来修正文稿，译者也一样。不过，使用不当时，这些工具也会给译文引入新问题。这种情况不常见，但一旦发生，就会损害最终成品的整体质量。

source.text: Flowey Speaks Again
source.raw: Flowey Speaks Again

translation.text: 再谈 Flowey 的说话方式

source.text: As we've already seen in the Japanese script, Flowey has used the boyish pronoun boku throughout the game so far. For first-time players, boku seems to reflect Flowey's friendly personality at the beginning of the game. However, there's another reason that Flowey uses boku: it turns out that he's actually the king's young son, stuck in the body of a flower.
source.raw:
As we've already seen in the Japanese script, Flowey has used the boyish
pronoun boku throughout the game so far. For first-time players, boku seems
to reflect Flowey's friendly personality at the beginning of the game. However,
there's another reason that Flowey uses boku: it turns out that he's actually the
king's young son, stuck in the body of a flower.

translation.text: 前面已经看到，日文版的 Flowey 到目前为止一直用带男孩气的第一人称 boku（我）。第一次玩的玩家，会觉得这很符合他在游戏开头表现出的友善性格。不过，还有另一个原因：他其实是国王年幼的儿子，被困在了一朵花的身体里。

source.raw:
Flowey uses the boyish pronoun 1K7(boku) at
the start of the game

translation.text: 游戏开头，Flowey 用带男孩气的「ボク」（boku，我）自称。

source.text: Flowey was actually a little boy before he got transformed, so it makes perfect sense for him to keep using boku
source.raw:
Flowey was actually a little boy before he got
transformed, so it makes perfect sense for him
to keep using boku

translation.text: Flowey 变身前其实是个小男孩，因此一直用 boku完全说得通。

source.text: In Japanese entertainment, it's normal for characters to switch to an aggressive personal pronoun after turning evil or being corrupted by immense power. In this case, however, Flowey continues to use the timid pronoun boku even after becoming a god-like entity:
source.raw:
In Japanese entertainment, it's normal for characters to switch to an aggressive
personal pronoun after turning evil or being corrupted by immense power. In
this case, however, Flowey continues to use the timid pronoun boku even after
becoming a god-like entity:

translation.text: 日本娱乐作品里，角色变坏或被强大力量腐蚀后，常会改用更咄咄逼人的自称。但 Flowey 即使变成近乎神明的存在，也仍用偏温弱的 boku：

source.text: Flowey continues to use boku even when he gets sinister
source.raw:
Flowey continues to use boku even when he
gets sinister

translation.text: 即使变得阴险，Flowey 仍用 boku。

source.text: Even when he's a terrifying creature of untold power, Flowey keeps using boku
source.raw:
Even when he's a terrifying creature of untold
power, Flowey keeps using boku

translation.text: 即使化为力量深不可测的恐怖生物，Flowey 仍用 boku。

source.text: Because the Japanese language has a wider variety of personal pronouns than the English language, this unwavering use of boku gives Japanese players an extra layer of insight into Flowey's character that isn't seen in the English script.
source.raw:
Because the Japanese language has a wider variety of personal pronouns than
the English language, this unwavering use of boku gives Japanese players an
extra layer of insight into Flowey's character that isn't seen in the English script.

translation.text: 日语人称代词比英语丰富得多，因此他始终不变的 boku，也让日本玩家多看见一层英文剧本无法直接体现的性格。

source.text: This scene offers another example of how the localization process can shine light on extra details that were there all along but were otherwise invisible. It's kind of like a microscope or a night-vision camera in that sense. In this chapter, we'll continue to see how pronouns enhance the Japanese dialogue.

source.text: Attitude Adjustment
source.raw: Attitude Adjustment

translation.text: 态度转变

source.text: When Sans says this out-of-character line during a No Mercy playthrough, he also switches to a very different font and uses proper punctuation
source.raw:
When Sans says this
out-of-character line
during a No Mercy
playthrough, he also

translation.text: Sans 在屠杀路线说出这句一反常态的话时，字体也完全变了，并开始规范使用标点。

source.text: Sans suddenly stops acting like a goofball, turns deadly serious, and begins to speak in an intimidating tone of voice. To preserve this attitude change in the Japanese script, the translator replaced his normal Japanese speech patterns with harsher speech patterns. For example, instead of his usual, laid-back personal pronoun oira, Sans now uses the more assertive pronoun ore. And instead of referring to the main character with the casual second-person pronoun an ta, he now uses the more condescending pronoun omae.
source.raw:
Sans suddenly stops acting like a goofball, turns deadly serious, and begins to
speak in an intimidating tone of voice. To preserve this attitude change in the
Japanese script, the translator replaced his normal Japanese speech patterns
with harsher speech patterns. For example, instead of his usual, laid-back
personal pronoun oira, Sans now uses the more assertive pronoun ore. And
instead of referring to the main character with the casual second-person
pronoun an ta, he now uses the more condescending pronoun omae.

translation.text: Sans 突然收起嬉皮笑脸，变得严肃而可怕，话语里满是威慑。为了保留这种态度转变，译者把他平时的日语说话方式改得更强硬。例如，原本随意的自称 oira（我）换成了更强势的 ore（我）；称呼主角时，也从较随便的 anta（你）变成了更居高临下的 omae（你）。

source.text: In many role-playing games, the player must earn "EXP" (short for "Experience Points") to increase their "LV" (short for "Level"). These standard terms appear in Undertale too, but it's eventually revealed that "EXP" and "LV" actually stand for "execution points" and "level of violence" here in the Underground.

for "execution points" and "level of violence" here in the Underground.

translation.text: 许多角色扮演游戏中，玩家要积累 EXP（Experience Points，经验值）来提升 LV（Level，等级）。《Undertale》也用了这些常见术语，但最后揭晓：在地下世界里，EXP 和 LV 其实分别代表 execution points（处决点数）和 level of violence（暴力等级）。

source.text: Because both of these surprise meanings rely on English abbreviations and English spelling, this wordplay would likely be lost in a straightforward, literal translation. To compensate for this, the localization team kept the English words mostly as-is, then included their Japanese meanings afterward for clarification. This solution preserves Toby's original intent without forcing Japanese words to awkwardly fit the English abbreviations.
source.raw:
Because both of these surprise meanings rely on English abbreviations and
English spelling, this wordplay would likely be lost in a straightforward, literal
translation. To compensate for this, the localization team kept the English
words mostly as-is, then included their Japanese meanings afterward for
clarification. This solution preserves Toby's original intent without forcing
Japanese words to awkwardly fit the English abbreviations.

translation.text: 这两处反转都依赖英语缩写和拼写，直接照字面翻译，很可能丢掉文字游戏。为此，团队基本保留了英文词语，再附上日语解释。这样既保留了 Toby 的意图，也不用勉强拼出能对应英语缩写的日语词。

surprise attack upon being spared. On the resulting game over screen, Sans

translation.text: 如果玩家能在 Sans 的攻击下撑得足够久，他就会显得疲惫不堪。这时，玩家可以选择饶恕他，而不是击败他。但这全是圈套：Sans 其实并没累，一被饶恕就会突然发动致命攻击。接着，在游戏结束画面里，他会用英文大喊：

source.raw: geeettttttt dunked on!!!

translation.text: geeettttttt dunked on!!!（被——隔扣了吧！！！）

source.text: In basketball, it's humiliating if someone performs a slam dunk over you. Thus the phrase "to be dunked on" is a humorous way of saying "you've been completely dominated" or "you're nothing to me". As it's a relatively new slang phrase and isn't often seen in video games, this surprise appearance adds extra humor to the line.
source.raw:
In basketball, it's humiliating if someone performs a slam dunk over you.
Thus the phrase "to be dunked on" is a humorous way of saying "you've been
completely dominated" or "you're nothing to me". As it's a relatively new slang
phrase and isn't often seen in video games, this surprise appearance adds extra
humor to the line.

translation.text: 篮球比赛中，被人隔着自己扣篮很丢脸。因此，“be dunked on”（被隔扣）也成了调侃人的说法，意思是“你被彻底碾压了”或“你在我眼里什么也不是”。这句俚语比较新，在游戏里又不常见，突然冒出来就更好笑了。

source.text: Unfortunately, there's no direct equivalent of the phrase "get dunked on" in Japanese. The localization team cycled through a number of potential Japanese replacements, most of which were variations on "ha, I fooled you" or insults based on Internet slang. Nothing quite had the same "bite" as the original English quote, however.
source.raw:
Unfortunately, there's no direct equivalent of the phrase "get dunked on" in
Japanese. The localization team cycled through a number of potential Japanese
replacements, most of which were variations on "ha, I fooled you" or insults
based on Internet slang. Nothing quite had the same "bite" as the original
English quote, however.

translation.text: 可惜，日语没有直接对应“get dunked on”的说法。团队尝试了好几个替代方案，多半是“哈，被我骗了吧”的各种变体，或来自网络用语的嘲讽。但都没有英文原句那股损劲儿。

source.text: As the project neared completion, Toby worked with the localization team to finally solve this conundrum. At Toby's suggestion, the team dropped Sans' English quote entirely and replaced it with something different but still suitable:
source.raw:
As the project neared completion, Toby worked with the localization team
to finally solve this conundrum. At Toby's suggestion, the team dropped
Sans' English quote entirely and replaced it with something different but still
suitable:

translation.text: 项目临近完成时，Toby 和团队终于解决了这个难题。按照 Toby 的建议，他们完全舍弃英文原句，换成意思不同、但同样合适的一句：

source.text: Huh? You died? That's weird. All I did was try to hug you ...
source.raw: Huh? You died? That's weird. All I did was try to hug you ...

translation.text: 咦？你死了？奇怪，我只是想抱抱你啊……

source.text: Even though this new line uses completely different wording to say something completely different, the reward is still the same for the player: a funny, memorable insult after a humiliating defeat.
source.raw:
Even though this new line uses completely different wording to say something
completely different, the reward is still the same for the player: a funny,
memorable insult after a humiliating defeat.

translation.text: 新台词的措辞与内容都完全变了，玩家得到的效果却一样：惨遭羞辱性失败后，又听到一句好笑、难忘的嘲讽。

source.text: Incidentally, when translators and creators work together like this to invent something new, some professional circles refer to the process as "transcreation" rather than "localization".
source.raw:
Incidentally, when translators and creators work together like this to
invent something new, some professional circles refer to the process as
"transcreation" rather than "localization".

translation.text: 顺带一提，译者和创作者像这样一起构思新内容，有些专业领域会称之为“创译”（transcreation），而不只是“本地化”。

source.text: It turns out that Torie! and Asgore once had a kindhearted child named Asriel. But through a series of tragic events, Asriel was transformed into the wrathful Flowey. Now, near the end of the game, Asriel gains immense, godlike power - enough for him to destroy everything and everyone for good.

enough for him to destroy everything and everyone for good.

translation.text: 原来，Toriel 和 Asgore 曾有个心地善良的孩子，名叫 Asriel。一连串悲剧却把他变成了满怀怨恨的 Flowey。如今游戏将近结尾，Asriel 获得了近乎神明的强大力量，足以彻底摧毁一切。

This localization choice offered two benefits: it retained the murderous

source.text: Of course, this localization choice had downsides too: players in Japan would know this important character by a very different last name, and the name Riiki doesn't evoke the same whimsical feeling that "Dreemur" does. More importantly, however, Toby chose the name "Asriel" with two other special meanings in mind:

Of course, this localization choice had downsides too: players in Japan would
know this important character by a very different last name, and the name

importantly, however, Toby chose the name "Asriel" with two other special

translation.text: 但它也有缺点：日本玩家会以一个完全不同的姓氏认识这位重要角色，而 Rāki 也没有“Dreemurr”那种梦幻感。更重要的是，Toby 取名“Asriel”时，还考虑了另外两层特殊含义：

source.text: "Asriel" is a reference to Azrael, the mythological angel of death
source.raw: "Asriel" is a reference to Azrael, the mythological angel of death

translation.text: • “Asriel”呼应神话中的死亡天使 Azrael。

source.text: "Asriel" is a combination of the names "Asgore" and "Torie]"
source.raw: "Asriel" is a combination of the names "Asgore" and "Torie]"

translation.text: • “Asriel”由“Asgore”和“Toriel”两个名字组合而成。

source.text: Everyone agreed that localizing "Asriel Dreemur" into a Japanese anagram brought more downsides than benefits. For this reason, the localization team dropped the anagrnm aspect of Asriel's name and kept his name in line with his original English name.
source.raw:
Everyone agreed that localizing "Asriel Dreemur" into a Japanese anagram
brought more downsides than benefits. For this reason, the localization team
dropped the anagrnm aspect of Asriel's name and kept his name in line with his
original English name.

translation.text: 大家一致认为，为“Asriel Dreemurr”另造日语重排名字弊大于利。因此，团队放弃了这一层文字游戏，让日文名与原来的英文名保持一致。

source.text: Asriel Speaks
source.raw: Asriel Speaks

translation.text: Asriel 的说话方式

source.text: During the big, final battle, Asriel speaks with strong conviction and disgust for the main character. To replicate this in Japanese, the translator gave Asriel a disrespectful speech pattern which includes the use of the assertive personal pronoun ore.
source.raw:
During the big, final battle, Asriel speaks with strong conviction and disgust
for the main character. To replicate this in Japanese, the translator gave
Asriel a disrespectful speech pattern which includes the use of the assertive
personal pronoun ore.

translation.text: 在最后的大战中，Asriel 说话非常笃定，对主角满怀厌恶。为在日语中再现这种感觉，译者让他采用无礼的语气，包括使用强势的第一人称 ore（我）。

source.text: In addition to using the first-person pronoun ore, Asriel uses the rude pronoun omae to say "you"
source.raw:
In addition to using
the first-person
pronoun ore, Asriel
uses the rude pronoun
omae to say "you"

translation.text: 除了用 ore自称，Asriel 还用不客气的 omae 来称呼“你”。

source.text: Little by little, though, the player is able to chip away at Asriel's hatred. Eventually, Asriel begins to speak with hesitation and less confidence. This is then followed by strong regret and shame for his actions.
source.raw:
Little by little, though, the player is able to chip away at Asriel's hatred.
Eventually, Asriel begins to speak with hesitation and less confidence. This is
then followed by strong regret and shame for his actions.

translation.text: 不过，玩家逐渐瓦解了 Asriel 的仇恨。他开始迟疑，不再那么自信，随后又对自己的行为深感懊悔和羞愧。

source.text: The translator paralleled this emotional change in Japanese by easing up on the disrespectful speech patterns. As part of this, Asriel eventually switches his personal pronoun to boku, which conveys a more innocent image befitting a scared young boy.
source.raw:
The translator paralleled this emotional change in Japanese by easing up on
the disrespectful speech patterns. As part of this, Asriel eventually switches his
personal pronoun to boku, which conveys a more innocent image befitting a
scared young boy.

translation.text: 译者也在日文中逐步缓和无礼的语气，呼应这种情感变化。Asriel 最后改用 boku（我）自称，呈现出更天真、符合受惊小男孩的形象。

source.text: Asriel switches to using boku to refer to himself, and the more familiar pronoun kimi to say "you"
source.raw:
Asriel switches to
using boku to refer to
himself, and the more
familiar pronoun kimi
to say "you"

translation.text: Asriel 改用 boku自称，并用较亲近的 kimi 来称呼“你”。

source.text: Because the original English text didn't include any such pronoun changes at all, it's clear that the translator viewed Asriel's dialogue through Asriel's eyes when translating his text, much as an actor might slip into their character's mindset before performing a scene.
source.raw:
Because the original English text didn't include any such pronoun changes at
all, it's clear that the translator viewed Asriel's dialogue through Asriel's eyes
when translating his text, much as an actor might slip into their character's
mindset before performing a scene.

translation.text: 英文原文没有这些代词变化，可见译者翻译时是从 Asriel 自己的视角理解台词的，就像演员上场前先进入角色的心境。

translation.text: 创作者与本地化人员如果缺乏密切合作，典故就很容易在翻译中丢失。

source.text: Asriel unleashes a powerful attack known as "Hyper Goner" in English. Toby noted that this is a reference to the final battle in Final Fantasy VI, in which the godlike villain uses his ultimate attack - known as "Goner" in English - when his defeat draws near. Toby also noted that it wasn't important to retain this reference in the Japanese script - he only asked that the Japanese name for "Hyper Goner" should sound "extremely powerful and cool".
source.raw:
Asriel unleashes a powerful attack known as "Hyper Goner" in English. Toby
noted that this is a reference to the final battle in Final Fantasy VI, in which the
godlike villain uses his ultimate attack - known as "Goner" in English - when
his defeat draws near. Toby also noted that it wasn't important to retain this
reference in the Japanese script - he only asked that the Japanese name for
"Hyper Goner" should sound "extremely powerful and cool".

translation.text: Asriel 会使出英文名为“Hyper Goner”的强力攻击。Toby 说明，这致敬的是《最终幻想 VI》的最终战：近乎神明的反派即将落败时，会使出英文名为“Goner”（意为“完蛋的人”）的终极攻击。Toby 也说，日文不一定要保留这个典故，只要求“Hyper Goner”的日文名听起来“强得不得了，而且很酷”。

source.text: The "Goner" attack in • Final Fantasy VI was originally known as "Missing" in Japanese
source.raw:
The "Goner" attack in •
Final Fantasy VI was
originally known as
"Missing" in Japanese

translation.text: 《最终幻想 VI》的“Goner”在日文原版里叫“Missing”（消失）。

source.text: Although it was unnecessary, the localizers did preserve this classic Final Fantasy reference. But because "Goner" was known in Japanese as "Missing", Asriel's "Hyper Goner" was localized into Japanese as "Hyper Missing".
source.raw:
Although it was unnecessary, the localizers did preserve this classic Final
Fantasy reference. But because "Goner" was known in Japanese as "Missing",
Asriel's "Hyper Goner" was localized into Japanese as "Hyper Missing".

translation.text: 虽然不是硬性要求，团队还是保留了这处对经典《最终幻想》的致敬。但因为“Goner”在日文里叫“Missing”，Asriel 的“Hyper Goner”便译成了“Hyper Missing”（超级消失）。

source.text: Umm ...
source.raw: Umm ...

source.text: Perhaps I should set these depressing topics aside and share a Japanese recipe instead. One of the best down-home recipes in Japan is Japanese curry. It's basically a warm, hearty stew with vegetables or meat or anything else, but with a rich, mouthwatering flavor. I want it to finally be popular where I'm from, so I hope you'll try making some sometime!
source.raw:
Perhaps I should set these depressing topics aside and share a Japanese
recipe instead. One of the best down-home recipes in Japan is Japanese
curry. It's basically a warm, hearty stew with vegetables or meat or
anything else, but with a rich, mouthwatering flavor. I want it to finally
be popular where I'm from, so I hope you'll try making some sometime!

translation.text: 或许该把这些沉重话题放一放，分享一道日本菜谱。日式咖喱是日本最棒的家常菜之一：把蔬菜、肉或其他食材炖成热腾腾、料足的浓汤，味道醇厚，叫人垂涎。我希望它也能在我的家乡流行起来，所以希望你有空也试着做一锅！

source.text: Toby explained that this short sentence carries two separate meanings:
source.raw: Toby explained that this short sentence carries two separate meanings:

source.raw: 1. "Refused" can mean "refused to die"

source.text: 2. "Refused" can mean "re-fused", referring to how the heart fragments fuse back together again
source.raw:
2. "Refused" can mean "re-fused", referring to how the heart fragments fuse
back together again

translation.text: 2. refused 也可拆成 re-fused（重新融合），呼应红心碎片再次聚合。

source.text: Toby understood that this pun would probably be difficult to retain in Japanese, so he noted that Meaning #l was more important to preserve. As a result, this line was given a straightforward to translation in early versions of the Japanese script:
source.raw:
Toby understood that this pun would probably be difficult to retain in Japanese,

source.text: But the SOUL couldn't be broken.
source.raw: But the SOUL couldn't be broken.

translation.text: 但灵魂无法被击碎。

source.text: After some more internal discussion, the localization team switched the line from an outside narrator's explanation to a first-person exclamation:
source.raw:
After some more internal discussion, the localization team switched the line
from an outside narrator's explanation to a first-person exclamation:

translation.text: 经过进一步内部讨论，团队把旁观叙述者的解释，改成了第一人称的呼喊：

source.text: No! I won't be broken!
source.raw: No! I won't be broken!

translation.text: 不！我才不会被击碎！

source.text: This Japanese wording - combined with the first-person perspective - evokes the sense of holding on to strong resolve against all odds, which is a common "final battle" theme in classic Japanese RPGs. Thus, the final Japanese line uses very different grammar and wording to parallel the meaning and intent of the original English line.
source.raw:
This Japanese wording - combined with the first-person perspective - evokes
the sense of holding on to strong resolve against all odds, which is a common
"final battle" theme in classic Japanese RPGs. Thus, the final Japanese line uses
very different grammar and wording to parallel the meaning and intent of the
original English line.

translation.text: 这套日语措辞配合第一人称视角，唤起了一种不论多大逆境也要坚持到底的决心，正是经典日式角色扮演游戏最终战中常见的主题。最终日文虽然采用了很不一样的语法与措辞，却对应了英文原句的含义和意图。

source.text: Multiple Saves
source.raw: Multiple Saves

translation.text: SAVE 的多重含义

source.text: It's revealed that whoever has the most "determination" in the Underground is able to use the in-game save menu functions. In other words, the most determined person in the Underground can freely load and save their progress. This is what allows the player to save and load their progress, just like in any other game. Except here, it's the actual, physical player's determination that enables this ability. The main character is just along for the ride.
source.raw:
It's revealed that whoever has the most "determination" in the Underground
is able to use the in-game save menu functions. In other words, the most
determined person in the Underground can freely load and save their progress.
This is what allows the player to save and load their progress, just like in any
other game. Except here, it's the actual, physical player's determination that
enables this ability. The main character is just along for the ride.

translation.text: 游戏揭晓，地下世界中“决心”最强的存在，能够使用存档菜单。换句话说，此人可以自由保存、读取进度。这也是玩家能像玩其他游戏一样存读档的原因；区别在于，这次赋予能力的是现实中玩家本人的决心，主角只是随之行动。

source.text: Toby begins by using "save" in a noun-like way related to computers
source.raw:
Toby begins by using
"save" in a noun-like
way related to
computers

translation.text: Toby 起初把 save 用作与电脑相关的名词，指存档。

source.text: During this final battle, Asriel absorbs and corrupts the souls of Sans, Papyrus, Undyne, and every other important story character. With all this new power, Asriel immobilizes the main character and takes control over the save menu. This becomes clear when the player reaches out for the save file, only to fail.
source.raw:
During this final battle, Asriel absorbs and corrupts the souls of Sans, Papyrus,
Undyne, and every other important story character. With all this new power,
Asriel immobilizes the main character and takes control over the save menu.
This becomes clear when the player reaches out for the save file, only to fail.

translation.text: 这场最终战中，Asriel 吸收并扭曲了 Sans、Papyrus、Undyne 以及其他重要角色的灵魂。获得这些力量后，他让主角动弹不得，也夺走了存档菜单的控制权。玩家伸手试图触及存档却失败时，这一点便显露出来。

source.text: Toby switches to using "save" as a verb and with a very different meaning
source.raw:
Toby switches to
using "save" as a
verb and with a very
different meaning

translation.text: 随后，Toby 把 save 改作动词，意义也大不相同：拯救。

source.text: After the player fails to reach the save file a second time, the game offers a hint about focusing on saving the characters whose souls have been absorbed:
source.raw:
After the player fails to reach the save file a second time, the game offers a hint
about focusing on saving the characters whose souls have been absorbed:

translation.text: 玩家第二次试图触及存档又失败后，游戏提示玩家转而拯救那些灵魂被吸收的角色：

source.text: You tried to reach your SAVE file. Nothing happened. You tried again to reach your SAVE file. Nothing happened.
source.raw:
You tried to reach your SAVE file. Nothing happened.
You tried again to reach your SAVE file. Nothing happened.

translation.text: 你试图触及自己的 SAVE 文件（存档）。什么也没有发生。你再次试图触及自己的 SAVE 文件。什么也没有发生。

source.text: But. .. Maybe, with what little power you have. .. You can SAVE something else.
source.raw:
But. .. Maybe, with what little power you have. ..
You can SAVE something else.

translation.text: 但是……也许，凭你仅剩的一点力量……你可以 SAVE（拯救）别的什么。

source.text: As we can see, the English word "save" in this scene carries multiple meanings:
source.raw: As we can see, the English word "save" in this scene carries multiple meanings:

translation.text: 可见，这里的英语词 save 承担了好几层含义：

source.text: "Save" is used to refer to the player's save file and the ability to load it
source.raw: "Save" is used to refer to the player's save file and the ability to load it

translation.text: • 指玩家的存档，以及读取存档的能力。

source.text: "Save" is used to mean "give salvation to someone's soul"
source.raw: "Save" is used to mean "give salvation to someone's soul"

translation.text: • 指“救赎某人的灵魂”。

source.text: "Save" is used to mean "to physically rescue someone"
source.raw: "Save" is used to mean "to physically rescue someone"

translation.text: • 指实际“救出某个人”。

source.text: Toby and the localization team spent a lot of time on preserving this wordplay in Japanese. After trying a number of solutions, the team settled on using the Japanese wordfukkatsu in place of"save". In general,fukkatsu means "to revive" or "to restore", but it can also be used to mean "to restore/load a saved file" and "to restore something back to how it should be".
source.raw:
Toby and the localization team spent a lot of time on preserving this wordplay
in Japanese. After trying a number of solutions, the team settled on using
the Japanese wordfukkatsu in place of"save". In general,fukkatsu means "to
revive" or "to restore", but it can also be used to mean "to restore/load a saved
file" and "to restore something back to how it should be".

translation.text: Toby 和本地化团队花了很多时间，试图在日语里保住这个文字游戏。尝试多种方案后，团队决定用日语 fukkatsu 替代 save。fukkatsu 通常表示“复活”或“恢复”，也可以用来表示“恢复／读取存档”以及“让事物恢复应有的状态”。

translation.text: 为了配合这个场景的新日语措辞，还得制作一个新的菜单图标。

source.text: Although the choice to replace "save" withft1kkatsll solved most of the wordplay issues, it also slightly altered the logic of the scene. To compensate for this change, the team added an extra line that bridges the jump from "save" to ft1kkatst1. Thus, the final Japanese scene became:
source.raw:
Although the choice to replace "save" withft1kkatsll solved most of the
wordplay issues, it also slightly altered the logic of the scene. To compensate
for this change, the team added an extra line that bridges the jump from "save"
to ft1kkatst1. Thus, the final Japanese scene became:

translation.text: 用 fukkatsu（复活、恢复）替换 save，虽然解决了大部分文字游戏问题，却也稍稍改变了场景逻辑。团队因此补上一句，衔接从“存档”到“恢复”的转折。最终日文场景变成了：

source.text: Yot1 reached for yol.lr save file. Bllt nothing happened. Yot1 reached for yow· save file again. Nothing happened. It appears yol.1 can't restore yow· save file after all.
source.raw:
Yot1 reached for yol.lr save file. Bllt nothing happened.
Yot1 reached for yow· save file again. Nothing happened.
It appears yol.1 can't restore yow· save file after all.

translation.text: 你向自己的存档伸出手。却什么也没有发生。你再次向存档伸出手。什么也没有发生。看来，终究无法恢复存档。

source.text: Bt1t ... Ify ol.1 gather what little power yol.1 have left ... Maybe yoll CAN restore something else.
source.raw:
Bt1t ... Ify ol.1 gather what little power yol.1 have left ...
Maybe yoll CAN restore something else.

translation.text: 但是……如果聚起你剩下的那一点力量……也许可以恢复别的什么。

source.text: This creative localization choice allowed the Japanese scene to approximate the wordplay in the original English scene. This choice did create new issues to be tackled, however:
source.raw:
This creative localization choice allowed the Japanese scene to approximate
the wordplay in the original English scene. This choice did create new issues to
be tackled, however:

translation.text: 这个有创意的方案，让日文场景接近了英文原场景的文字游戏。不过，它也带来了新问题：

source.text: 1. The in-game "SAVE" icon needed to be redrawn to say ft1kkatStl in Japanese
source.raw:
1. The in-game "SAVE" icon needed to be redrawn to say ft1kkatStl in
Japanese

translation.text: 1. 游戏中的“SAVE”图标需要重画，改成日语 fukkatsu（复活）。

source.text: 2. The new icon needed extra programming to load properly based on the player's chosen language
source.raw:
2. The new icon needed extra programming to load properly based on the
player's chosen language

translation.text: 2. 要额外编写程序，让新图标按玩家所选语言正确加载。

source.text: 3. Dropping the word "SAVE" from the scene broke the connection to "SAVE the World", the official English title of this scene's background music track
source.raw:
3. Dropping the word "SAVE" from the scene broke the connection to
"SAVE the World", the official English title of this scene's background
music track

translation.text: 3. 场景中不再出现“SAVE”后，也就失去了与背景音乐官方英文曲名“SAVE the World”（拯救世界）的联系。

source.text: The localization team easily fixed the first two issues. The third issue came into play a year after Undertale's Japanese release, when the game's official soundtrack was set to be released in Japan. Because this track is so iconic and memorable, Toby requested that the Japanese soundtrack retain the "SAVE the World" name as-is rather than replace it with a less memorable pun onfukkatsl.1.
source.raw:
The localization team easily fixed the first two issues. The third issue came
into play a year after Undertale's Japanese release, when the game's official
soundtrack was set to be released in Japan. Because this track is so iconic and
memorable, Toby requested that the Japanese soundtrack retain the "SAVE the
World" name as-is rather than replace it with a less memorable pun onfukkatsl.1.

translation.text: 前两个问题很容易解决。第三个问题，则在《Undertale》日版推出一年后、官方原声带准备在日本发行时显现出来。因为这首曲子太有代表性、太令人难忘，Toby 要求日版原声带原样保留“SAVE the World”，不要换成一个不如原名好记的 fukkatsu 双关。

source.text: Every choice you ever make as a translator or localizer has the potential to bite you in the butt years later in unexpected ways
source.raw:
Every choice you ever

unexpected ways

translation.text: 译者或本地化人员做出的每个选择，都可能几年后以意想不到的方式反过来给自己找麻烦。

source.raw:
In some English-speaking cultures, it's common for parents to punish their
children by sending them to their room. This punishment is less common in

translation.text: 在一些英语文化中，家长常用“回房间去”来惩罚孩子。但日本不太常用这种处罚，因此日文里的 Undyne 给 Papyrus 换了个稍有不同的惩罚：

source.raw: Don't give me that back-talk! Go to your room and sit down seiza-style!
